column6: Shìzhǎng yīxíng cānguān le gōngchǎng.
column7: The mayor and his party visited the factory.
column9: After a leader's name it means that person and the party with them: 市長一行 is the mayor and his delegation, common in news. Read yī xíng; 一行 as 'one row' is yī háng.

column3: Square meters, often shortened to 平 in speech (八十平). In Taiwan the meter is usually 公尺, as in 平方公尺, and homes are measured in 坪.
column4: 这套房子有八十平方米。
column5: 這套房子有八十平方米。
column6: Zhè tào fángzi yǒu bāshí píngfāngmǐ.
column7: This apartment is eighty square meters.
column9: Square meters, often shortened to 平 in speech (八十平). In Taiwan the meter is usually 公尺, as in 平方公尺, and homes are measured in 坪.

column3: The simplified 杆 covers two readings: gǎn for a stick or shaft and the measure word for guns (笔杆, 一杆枪), and gān for a pole (旗杆, 栏杆). Read it by the word it sits in.
column4: 他手里握着一杆枪。
column5: 他手裡握著一桿槍。
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ wòzhe yī gǎn qiāng.
column7: He held a rifle in his hand.
column9: Read gǎn, 桿 is a stick or shaft and the measure word for guns (筆桿, 一桿槍); a pole read gān is usually written 杆, as in 欄杆.

column3: One generation or era. 新一代 is the new generation of people or products (新一代手机); 年轻一代 and 下一代 are the young and the next generation.
column4: 新一代手机已经上市了。
column5: 新一代手機已經上市了。
column6: Xīn yīdài shǒujī yǐjīng shàngshì le.
column7: The new generation of phones is already on sale.
column9: One generation or era. 新一代 is the new generation of people or products (新一代手機); 年輕一代 and 下一代 are the young and the next generation.

column3: A large batch of people or goods, put before the noun: 大批游客, 大批货物. It does not work as a predicate on its own. 大 is a picture of a person standing facing forward.
column4: 大批游客涌入了这座小城。
column5: 大批遊客湧入了這座小城。
column6: Dàpī yóukè yǒngrù le zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
column7: Large numbers of tourists poured into this small city.
column9: A large batch of people or goods, put before the noun: 大批遊客, 大批貨物. It does not work as a predicate on its own. 大 is a picture of a person standing facing forward.

column3: The vast majority. 绝 adds 'by far' to 大多数 (most), and it is followed by people or parts: 绝大多数人, 绝大部分. One scholar suggests 多 is two pieces of meat 肉: meat was scarce, so two pieces meant a lot.
column4: 绝大多数学生都通过了考试。
column5: 絕大多數學生都通過了考試。
column6: Juédàduōshù xuéshēng dōu tōngguò le kǎoshì.
column7: The vast majority of the students passed the exam.
column9: The vast majority. 絕 adds 'by far' to 大多數 (most), and it is followed by people or parts: 絕大多數人, 絕大部分. One scholar suggests 多 is two pieces of meat 肉: meat was scarce, so two pieces meant a lot.

column3: The total amount of something taken as a whole, in economics and statistics: 能源消费总量, 进口总量, and 总量控制 (capping the total).
column4: 这个城市的用水总量在增加。
column5: 這個城市的用水總量在增加。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de yòngshuǐ zǒngliàng zài zēngjiā.
column7: The total water use of this city is increasing.
column9: The total amount of something taken as a whole, in economics and statistics: 能源消費總量, 進口總量, and 總量控制 (capping the total).

column3: A written way to say 'all sorts of', usually before abstract nouns and without 的: 种种原因, 种种困难, 种种迹象.
column4: 由于种种原因，会议推迟了。
column5: 由於種種原因，會議推遲了。
column6: Yóuyú zhǒngzhǒng yuányīn, huìyì tuīchí le.
column7: For various reasons, the meeting was postponed.
column9: A written way to say 'all sorts of', usually before abstract nouns and without 的: 種種原因, 種種困難, 種種跡象.

column3: The gap between two percentages: from 5% to 7% is two 百分点, not 40%. Common in economic news. 分 shows a knife 刀 separating something (八).
column4: 失业率上升了两个百分点。
column5: 失業率上升了兩個百分點。
column6: Shīyèlǜ shàngshēng le liǎng gè bǎifēndiǎn.
column7: The unemployment rate rose by two percentage points.
column9: The gap between two percentages: from 5% to 7% is two 百分點, not 40%. Common in economic news. 分 shows a knife 刀 separating something (八).

column3: An index for anything rated by number: 股票指数, 物价指数, 空气质量指数, 紫外线指数. In math it is the exponent.
column4: 今天的紫外线指数很高。
column5: 今天的紫外線指數很高。
column6: Jīntiān de zǐwàixiàn zhǐshù hěn gāo.
column7: The UV index is very high today.
column9: An index for anything rated by number: 股票指數, 物價指數, 空氣質量指數, 紫外線指數. In math it is the exponent.

column3: The written and mathematical 'less than' (<), with 大于 for '>'. In ordinary speech you say 比…小 instead.
column4: 年龄小于十八岁的人不能进入。
column5: 年齡小於十八歲的人不能進入。
column6: Niánlíng xiǎoyú shíbā suì de rén bùnéng jìnrù.
column7: People under eighteen may not enter.
column9: The written and mathematical 'less than' (<), with 大於 for '>'. In ordinary speech you say 比…小 instead.

column3: 'In many respects': 在多方面, 多方面的 (many-sided), or before a verb, 多方面努力 (effort on several fronts). 面 began as a picture of a face, with the eye drawn larger.
column4: 这个问题需要从多方面来考虑。
column5: 這個問題需要從多方面來考慮。
column6: Zhège wèntí xūyào cóng duōfāngmiàn lái kǎolǜ.
column7: This question needs to be considered from many angles.
column9: 'In many respects': 在多方面, 多方面的 (many-sided), or before a verb, 多方面努力 (effort on several fronts). 面 began as a picture of a face, with the eye drawn larger.

column3: A surprise that is always pleasant: 给你一个惊喜, and 惊喜 also works as an adjective or a verb. 喜 combines a drum with a mouth.
column4: 生日那天，朋友给了我一个惊喜。
column5: 生日那天，朋友給了我一個驚喜。
column6: Shēngrì nà tiān, péngyou gěi le wǒ yī gè jīngxǐ.
column7: On my birthday, a friend gave me a nice surprise.
column9: A surprise that is always pleasant: 給你一個驚喜, and 驚喜 also works as an adjective or a verb. 驚 has a horse 馬, since horses are easily startled. 喜 combines a drum with a mouth.

column3: Being alone in a deep, lasting way. It describes a person, a life or a feeling: 孤独感, 孤独的生活, 孤独终老 (to die alone).
column4: 他一个人住在山里，过着孤独的生活。
column5: 他一個人住在山裡，過著孤獨的生活。
column6: Tā yī gè rén zhù zài shān lǐ, guòzhe gūdú de shēnghuó.
column7: He lives alone in the mountains, leading a solitary life.
column9: Being alone in a deep, lasting way. It describes a person, a life or a feeling: 孤獨感, 孤獨的生活, 孤獨終老 (to die alone).

column3: Worry about a situation, more formal than 担心 and common in news: 令人担忧 (worrying), 表示担忧 (to voice concern).
column4: 专家对经济前景表示担忧。
column5: 專家對經濟前景表示擔憂。
column6: Zhuānjiā duì jīngjì qiánjǐng biǎoshì dānyōu.
column7: Experts voiced concern about the economic outlook.
column9: Worry about a situation, more formal than 擔心 and common in news: 令人擔憂 (worrying), 表示擔憂 (to voice concern).

column3: For fates, lives and scenes that are tragic, not for a passing sad mood: 悲惨的命运, 悲惨的遭遇, 场面悲惨.
column4: 这部电影讲了一个悲惨的故事。
column5: 這部電影講了一個悲慘的故事。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng le yī gè bēicǎn de gùshi.
column7: This film tells a tragic story.
column9: For fates, lives and scenes that are tragic, not for a passing sad mood: 悲慘的命運, 悲慘的遭遇, 場面悲慘.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 发了怒, 发什么怒. 发 here means to let out a feeling, as in 发火, 发脾气, 发愁.
column4: 老板一听就发怒了。
column5: 老闆一聽就發怒了。
column6: Lǎobǎn yī tīng jiù fānù le.
column7: The boss flew into a rage as soon as he heard.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 發了怒, 發什麼怒. 發 here means to let out a feeling, as in 發火, 發脾氣, 發愁.

column3: A verb plus object, so you heave a sigh: 叹了一口气, 叹口气. The sigh comes from sadness, helplessness or relief.
column4: 别叹气了，明天会更好。
column5: 別嘆氣了，明天會更好。
column6: Bié tànqì le, míngtiān huì gèng hǎo.
column7: Stop sighing; tomorrow will be better.
column9: A verb plus object, so you heave a sigh: 嘆了一口氣, 嘆口氣. The sigh comes from sadness, helplessness or relief.

column3: To touch someone's feelings or win them over. The person moved is the object or the subject of 被: 打动人心, 被…打动.
column4: 这首歌打动了很多人。
column5: 這首歌打動了很多人。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē dǎdòng le hěn duō rén.
column7: This song moved many people.
column9: To touch someone's feelings or win them over. The person moved is the object or the subject of 被: 打動人心, 被…打動.

column3: Mostly before a noun: 难忘的一天, or 令人难忘, 终生难忘. 难 before a verb means hard to do it (难懂, 难忘) or unpleasant to (难吃 tastes bad, 难看 ugly).
column4: 那是一个难忘的夜晚。
column5: 那是一個難忘的夜晚。
column6: Nà shì yī gè nánwàng de yèwǎn.
column7: That was an unforgettable evening.
column9: Mostly before a noun: 難忘的一天, or 令人難忘, 終生難忘. 難 before a verb means hard to do it (難懂, 難忘) or unpleasant to (難吃 tastes bad, 難看 ugly).

column3: A heartfelt wish you hope to fulfill: 实现心愿, 了却心愿 (to settle a long-held wish). More personal than 愿望.
column4: 我的心愿是环游世界。
column5: 我的心願是環遊世界。
column6: Wǒ de xīnyuàn shì huányóu shìjiè.
column7: My wish is to travel around the world.
column9: A heartfelt wish you hope to fulfill: 實現心願, 了卻心願 (to settle a long-held wish). More personal than 願望.

column3: Formal letter closing: it sits on its own line near the end, and the salutation, usually 敬礼, goes on the next line.
column4: 信的最后，他写上了“此致敬礼”。
column5: 信的最後，他寫上了「此致敬禮」。
column6: Xìn de zuìhòu, tā xiě shàng le “cǐzhì jìnglǐ”.
column7: At the end of the letter he wrote the formal closing.
column9: Formal letter closing: it sits on its own line near the end, and the salutation, usually 敬禮, goes on the next line.

column3: Used to address a group, typically at the start of a speech or announcement. It is polite and a little formal, and never used for one person.
column4: 诸位请坐。
column5: 諸位請坐。
column6: Zhūwèi qǐng zuò.
column7: Everyone, please sit down.
column9: Used to address a group, typically at the start of a speech or announcement. It is polite and a little formal, and never used for one person.

column3: A verb plus its object: the person who gets the seat comes first with 给, as in 给老人让座. It is the standard phrase for giving up your seat on a bus or train. 座 is formed from the word for sitting and is literally “that which is sat on”.
column4: 他给老人让座了。
column5: 他給老人讓座了。
column6: Tā gěi lǎorén ràngzuò le.
column7: He gave up his seat to an elderly person.
column9: A verb plus its object: the person who gets the seat comes first with 給, as in 給老人讓座. It is the standard phrase for giving up your seat on a bus or train. 座 is formed from the word for sitting and is literally “that which is sat on”.

column3: The object is usually a group that needs care: 关爱儿童, 关爱老人. It is warm and a little formal, the tone of campaigns, schools and speeches rather than a word between friends.
column4: 我们要关爱老人。
column5: 我們要關愛老人。
column6: Wǒmen yào guān'ài lǎorén.
column7: We should care for the elderly.
column9: The object is usually a group that needs care: 關愛兒童, 關愛老人. It is warm and a little formal, the tone of campaigns, schools and speeches rather than a word between friends.

column3: Describes the loyalty of a servant, soldier, official or pet to a master or country: 对主人忠心. The set phrase 忠心耿耿 means loyal to the core.
column4: 这只狗对主人很忠心。
column5: 這隻狗對主人很忠心。
column6: Zhè zhī gǒu duì zhǔrén hěn zhōngxīn.
column7: This dog is very loyal to its owner.
column9: Describes the loyalty of a servant, soldier, official or pet to a master or country: 對主人忠心. The set phrase 忠心耿耿 means loyal to the core.

column3: Describes what is surprising in a delightful or mysterious way, often before a noun with 的: 奇妙的世界, 奇妙的感觉, 奇妙的缘分. It does not simply mean excellent.
column4: 这是一次奇妙的旅行。
column5: 這是一次奇妙的旅行。
column6: Zhè shì yī cì qímiào de lǚxíng.
column7: This was a wonderful trip.
column9: Describes what is surprising in a delightful or mysterious way, often before a noun with 的: 奇妙的世界, 奇妙的感覺, 奇妙的緣分. It does not simply mean excellent.

column3: Used for sights on a grand scale that fill the eye: a waterfall, a mountain range, a parade, a skyline. Size and force are the point, not prettiness.
column4: 瀑布的景象十分壮观。
column5: 瀑布的景象十分壯觀。
column6: Pùbù de jǐngxiàng shífēn zhuàngguān.
column7: The sight of the waterfall is magnificent.
column9: Used for sights on a grand scale that fill the eye: a waterfall, a mountain range, a parade, a skyline. Size and force are the point, not prettiness.

column3: Describes the thing that moves you, not the person who is moved: a story, a scene or a speech is 感人, while you are 感动. Common before a noun: 感人的故事.
column4: 这个故事很感人。
column5: 這個故事很感人。
column6: Zhè ge gùshi hěn gǎnrén.
column7: This story is very touching.
column9: Describes the thing that moves you, not the person who is moved: a story, a scene or a speech is 感人, while you are 感動. Common before a noun: 感人的故事.

column3: Praise for a person or an achievement: 杰出的科学家, 杰出贡献. It is formal, the language of news, awards and speeches rather than casual talk. In its oldest form 出 showed a foot 止 stepping out of a cave 凵.
column4: 他是一位杰出的科学家。
column5: 他是一位傑出的科學家。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi jiéchū de kēxuéjiā.
column7: He is an outstanding scientist.
column9: Praise for a person or an achievement: 傑出的科學家, 傑出貢獻. It is formal, the language of news, awards and speeches rather than casual talk. In its oldest form 出 showed a foot 止 stepping out of a cave 凵.

column3: Used before a noun for people, brands and companies that many have heard of: 知名企业, 知名作家. It is formal; in everyday talk 有名 is more usual. One explanation: 名 puts a moon 夕 and a mouth 口 together, saying your name to identify yourself in the dark.
column4: 他是一位知名的作家。
column5: 他是一位知名的作家。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi zhīmíng de zuòjiā.
column7: He is a well-known writer.
column9: Used before a noun for people, brands and companies that many have heard of: 知名企業, 知名作家. It is formal; in everyday talk 有名 is more usual. One explanation: 名 puts a moon 夕 and a mouth 口 together, saying your name to identify yourself in the dark.

column3: Mostly a building block: 精彩, 精神, 精确, 精力, 妖精. On its own in speech it means shrewd, quick to look after one's own interests: 他很精.
column4: 他做生意很精。
column5: 他做生意很精。
column6: Tā zuò shēngyi hěn jīng.
column7: He is shrewd in business.
column9: Mostly a building block: 精彩, 精神, 精確, 精力, 妖精. On its own in speech it means shrewd, quick to look after one's own interests: 他很精.

column3: Describes goods and services, such as 优质产品, 优质服务 and 优质大米; it is the usual word on labels and in ads. The opposite is 劣质.
column4: 这家店只卖优质水果。
column5: 這家店只賣優質水果。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ mài yōuzhì shuǐguǒ.
column7: This shop sells only high-quality fruit.
column9: Describes goods and services, such as 優質產品, 優質服務 and 優質大米; it is the usual word on labels and in ads. The opposite is 劣質.

column3: The good name you can protect or damage: 损害名誉, 名誉受损. Before a title it means honorary: 名誉教授, 名誉主席.
column4: 他很爱惜自己的名誉。
column5: 他很愛惜自己的名譽。
column6: Tā hěn àixī zìjǐ de míngyù.
column7: He guards his reputation carefully.
column9: The good name you can protect or damage: 損害名譽, 名譽受損. Before a title it means honorary: 名譽教授, 名譽主席.

column3: Playfully naughty, said of children and young animals, with more affection than anger; 调皮 is the closest everyday word. 皮 is drawn as a hand stripping the fur from an animal pelt.
column4: 这个孩子很顽皮。
column5: 這個孩子很頑皮。
column6: Zhè ge háizi hěn wánpí.
column7: This child is very naughty.
column9: Playfully naughty, said of children and young animals, with more affection than anger; 調皮 is the closest everyday word. 皮 is drawn as a hand stripping the fur from an animal pelt.

column3: Admiring: it praises will, life or resistance that does not give in, as in 顽强的意志 and 顽强拼搏. Its near twin 顽固 is stubborn as a fault.
column4: 他顽强地活了下来。
column5: 他頑強地活了下來。
column6: Tā wánqiáng de huó le xiàlái.
column7: He held on and survived against the odds.
column9: Admiring: it praises will, life or resistance that does not give in, as in 頑強的意志 and 頑強拼搏. Its near twin 頑固 is stubborn as a fault.

column3: Sounds the same as 很 (very) but means fierce and ruthless; you meet it in 凶狠, 狠心 (hard-hearted) and 狠狠地 (fiercely). It can also mean doing something with all one's force.
column4: 他对自己真狠。
column5: 他對自己真狠。
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ zhēn hěn.
column7: He is really hard on himself.
column9: Sounds the same as 很 (very) but means fierce and ruthless; you meet it in 兇狠, 狠心 (hard-hearted) and 狠狠地 (fiercely). It can also mean doing something with all one's force.

column3: The sense heard every day is the loanword “cool”: 很酷, 太酷了. The old sense of harsh and cruel lives on in compounds such as 残酷 and 酷刑.
column4: 这个发型很酷。
column5: 這個髮型很酷。
column6: Zhè ge fàxíng hěn kù.
column7: This hairstyle is cool.
column9: The sense heard every day is the loanword “cool”: 很酷, 太酷了. The old sense of harsh and cruel lives on in compounds such as 殘酷 and 酷刑.

column3: Fits things as well as people: 残酷的现实, 残酷的竞争, 残酷的战争. For a person who is cold and unfeeling, 冷酷 is the usual word.
column4: 现实有时很残酷。
column5: 現實有時很殘酷。
column6: Xiànshí yǒushí hěn cánkù.
column7: Reality can be cruel at times.
column9: Fits things as well as people: 殘酷的現實, 殘酷的競爭, 殘酷的戰爭. For a person who is cold and unfeeling, 冷酷 is the usual word.

column3: Often kind: it describes ordinary people and humble lives with respect, as in 平凡的岗位 or 平凡中见伟大. The critical word for mediocre is 平庸.
column4: 他是个平凡的人，但很善良。
column5: 他是個平凡的人，但很善良。
column6: Tā shì ge píngfán de rén, dàn hěn shànliáng.
column7: He is an ordinary person, but a kind one.
column9: Often kind: it describes ordinary people and humble lives with respect, as in 平凡的崗位 or 平凡中見偉大. The critical word for mediocre is 平庸.

column3: Two senses: steady and down-to-earth in work (他做事很踏实), and at ease in the mind (心里踏实). Pronounced tāshi on the mainland and tàshí in Taiwan.
column4: 他做事很踏实。
column5: 他做事很踏實。
column6: Tā zuò shì hěn tāshi.
column7: He works in a steady, down-to-earth way.
column9: Two senses: steady and down-to-earth in work (他做事很踏實), and at ease in the mind (心裡踏實). Pronounced tāshi on the mainland and tàshí in Taiwan.

column3: A written, slightly formal verb that always takes another verb after it: 敢于承认, 敢于挑战. Speech uses plain 敢, and 敢于 praises courage. In its oldest form 敢 showed a hand using a capturing tool to hunt a wild boar.
column4: 我们要敢于面对困难。
column5: 我們要敢於面對困難。
column6: Wǒmen yào gǎnyú miànduì kùnnan.
column7: We must dare to face difficulties.
column9: A written, slightly formal verb that always takes another verb after it: 敢於承認, 敢於挑戰. Speech uses plain 敢, and 敢於 praises courage. In its oldest form 敢 showed a hand using a capturing tool to hunt a wild boar.

column3: Describes a dominant party, as in 强势品牌 and 强势货币. Of a person it can mean pushy or domineering, so it is not always praise.
column4: 他在谈判中很强势。
column5: 他在談判中很強勢。
column6: Tā zài tánpàn zhōng hěn qiángshì.
column7: He was very forceful in the negotiation.
column9: Describes a dominant party, as in 強勢品牌 and 強勢貨幣. Of a person it can mean pushy or domineering, so it is not always praise.

column3: Physical strength of a body: people, animals, muscles. Strength of a country or a company is 强大, not 强壮. Its older form 彊 was built with a bow 弓, because “Bow is powerful.”
column4: 他长得又高又强壮。
column5: 他長得又高又強壯。
column6: Tā zhǎng de yòu gāo yòu qiángzhuàng.
column7: He is tall and strong.
column9: Physical strength of a body: people, animals, muscles. Strength of a country or a company is 強大, not 強壯. Its older form 彊 was built with a bow 弓, because “Bow is powerful.”

column3: The word for turning a corner when giving directions: 往左拐, 在路口拐弯. It also means to kidnap or swindle, as in 拐骗, and gives 拐杖 (a walking stick).
column4: 到前面路口往左拐。
column5: 到前面路口往左拐。
column6: Dào qiánmiàn lùkǒu wǎng zuǒ guǎi.
column7: Turn left at the intersection ahead.
column9: The word for turning a corner when giving directions: 往左拐, 在路口拐彎. It also means to kidnap or swindle, as in 拐騙, and gives 拐杖 (a walking stick).

column3: To tilt the head back: 仰头看, 仰望, 仰卧 (lie on one's back). Looking up becomes respect in 敬仰 and 仰慕, and belief in 信仰.
column4: 他仰头看着天空。
column5: 他仰頭看著天空。
column6: Tā yǎng tóu kàn zhe tiānkōng.
column7: He looked up at the sky.
column9: To tilt the head back: 仰頭看, 仰望, 仰臥 (lie on one's back). Looking up becomes respect in 敬仰 and 仰慕, and belief in 信仰.

column3: Both literal (低头看手机) and figurative: 向困难低头 means to give in to difficulties, and 不低头 means refusing to yield.
column4: 他低头看手机。
column5: 他低頭看手機。
column6: Tā dītóu kàn shǒujī.
column7: He looks down at his phone.
column9: Both literal (低頭看手機) and figurative: 向困難低頭 means to give in to difficulties, and 不低頭 means refusing to yield.

column3: Turning or twisting that strains: 扭头 turns the head away, 扭伤 is a sprain, and 扭转 turns a situation around.
column4: 我的脚扭了。
column5: 我的腳扭了。
column6: Wǒ de jiǎo niǔ le.
column7: I twisted my ankle.
column9: Turning or twisting that strains: 扭頭 turns the head away, 扭傷 is a sprain, and 扭轉 turns a situation around.

column3: Fits things with length: roads, rivers, wires, a spine (弯曲的小路, 脊柱弯曲). A person bending at the waist is 弯腰 instead. 曲 is drawn as a bent object.
column4: 这条路弯曲得很厉害。
column5: 這條路彎曲得很厲害。
column6: Zhè tiáo lù wānqū de hěn lìhai.
column7: This road winds a lot.
column9: Fits things with length: roads, rivers, wires, a spine (彎曲的小路, 脊柱彎曲). A person bending at the waist is 彎腰 instead. 曲 is drawn as a bent object.

column3: To hold up from below with the palm: 托着下巴 is resting your chin on your hand. It also means to ask a favor, as in 托你一件事 and 拜托.
column4: 他用手托着下巴。
column5: 他用手托著下巴。
column6: Tā yòng shǒu tuō zhe xiàba.
column7: He rests his chin on his hand.
column9: To hold up from below with the palm: 托著下巴 is resting your chin on your hand. It also means to ask a favor, as in 托你一件事 and 拜託.

column3: The 走 shows the thing leaving the speaker's place: 拿走 is take it away, while 拿来 is bring it here. 走 began as a picture of a running man.
column4: 请不要拿走别人的东西。
column5: 請不要拿走別人的東西。
column6: Qǐng bù yào názǒu biérén de dōngxi.
column7: Please do not take other people's things.
column9: The 走 shows the thing leaving the speaker's place: 拿走 is take it away, while 拿來 is bring it here. 走 began as a picture of a running man.

column3: With this reading, 背着 usually means doing something behind someone's back: 背着父母, 背着我. Hands held behind the back is 背着手. Carrying a load on the back is the other reading, bēizhe.
column4: 他背着父母偷偷出去了。
column5: 他背著父母偷偷出去了。
column6: Tā bèizhe fùmǔ tōutōu chūqù le.
column7: He slipped out behind his parents' backs.
column9: With this reading, 背著 usually means doing something behind someone's back: 背著父母, 背著我. Hands held behind the back is 背著手. Carrying a load on the back is the other reading, bēizhe.

column3: 着 makes the pointing last while something else happens: 指着地图说, 指着我问. The thing pointed at follows directly; 指着鼻子骂 is rude, scolding someone to their face.
column4: 他指着地图问我们在哪儿。
column5: 他指著地圖問我們在哪兒。
column6: Tā zhǐzhe dìtú wèn wǒmen zài nǎr.
column7: He pointed at the map and asked where we were.
column9: 著 makes the pointing last while something else happens: 指著地圖說, 指著我問. The thing pointed at follows directly; 指著鼻子罵 is rude, scolding someone to their face.

column3: To be right up against something: 挨着窗户坐, 紧挨着. The same 挨 read ái means to suffer, as in 挨骂 and 挨打, so the reading matters.
column4: 他挨着我坐下了。
column5: 他挨著我坐下了。
column6: Tā āizhe wǒ zuò xià le.
column7: He sat down next to me.
column9: To be right up against something: 挨著窗戶坐, 緊挨著. The same 挨 read ái means to suffer, as in 挨罵 and 挨打, so the reading matters.

column3: Read zhā for pricking and settling in: 扎针 (get a shot or acupuncture), 扎根 (take root), 扎营. Other readings are zā, to tie (扎辫子), and zhá in 挣扎.
column4: 手指被针扎了一下。
column5: 手指被針扎了一下。
column6: Shǒuzhǐ bèi zhēn zhā le yī xià.
column7: A needle pricked my finger.
column9: Read zhā for pricking and settling in: 扎針 (get a shot or acupuncture), 扎根 (take root), 紮營. Other readings are zā, to tie (扎辮子), and zhá in 掙扎.

column3: Adds something extra to what is already there: 添饭 (a refill of rice), 添水, 添麻烦 (to trouble someone). In math and for plain addition the word is 加.
column4: 请再给我添点水。
column5: 請再給我添點水。
column6: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ tiān diǎn shuǐ.
column7: Please top up my water.
column9: Adds something extra to what is already there: 添飯 (a refill of rice), 添水, 添麻煩 (to trouble someone). In math and for plain addition the word is 加.

column3: Read chòng, it means facing or aimed at someone: 冲着他笑, 冲我来. It also means strong or pungent, as in 味儿很冲. The common reading chōng is to rush, rinse or flush.
column4: 她冲我笑了笑。
column5: 她衝我笑了笑。
column6: Tā chòng wǒ xiào le xiào.
column7: She smiled at me.
column9: Read chòng, it means facing or aimed at someone: 衝著他笑, 衝我來. It also means strong or pungent, as in 味兒很衝. The common reading chōng is to rush, rinse or flush.

column3: Rarely used alone. It is mostly a suffix naming a shape, as in 圆形, 三角形, 长方形, or sits in words such as 形状, 形成, 情形.
column4: 这张桌子是圆形的。
column5: 這張桌子是圓形的。
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì yuán xíng de.
column7: This table is round.
column9: Rarely used alone. It is mostly a suffix naming a shape, as in 圓形, 三角形, 長方形, or sits in words such as 形狀, 形成, 情形.

column3: Either an accident or a trick: things warp from heat, water or pressure (木门变形), and 变形金刚 is the Transformers toys and films.
column4: 木门被水泡得变形了。
column5: 木門被水泡得變形了。
column6: Mùmén bèi shuǐ pào de biànxíng le.
column7: The wooden door warped from soaking in water.
column9: Either an accident or a trick: things warp from heat, water or pressure (木門變形), and 變形金剛 is the Transformers toys and films.

column3: Spacious and open: roads, squares, rivers, the sea, and figuratively a broad mind (胸怀宽阔). It gives a feeling of open space, not a measurement.
column4: 这条路又直又宽阔。
column5: 這條路又直又寬闊。
column6: Zhè tiáo lù yòu zhí yòu kuānkuò.
column7: This road is straight and wide.
column9: Spacious and open: roads, squares, rivers, the sea, and figuratively a broad mind (胸懷寬闊). It gives a feeling of open space, not a measurement.

column3: Rarely a word on its own: wide inside 宽阔, 广阔 and 辽阔. In speech it also means newly rich and showy, as in 阔气 and 阔起来.
column4: 他发财以后就阔起来了。
column5: 他發財以後就闊起來了。
column6: Tā fācái yǐhòu jiù kuò qǐlái le.
column7: After he got rich, he began living it up.
column9: Rarely a word on its own: wide inside 寬闊, 廣闊 and 遼闊. In speech it also means newly rich and showy, as in 闊氣 and 闊起來.

column3: Grand in scale and ambition: 宏大的计划, 宏大的规模, 宏大的场面. It is written and slightly formal, and it stresses grandeur rather than plain size: a building can be 宏大, but a big apple is just 大.
column4: 他们有一个宏大的计划。
column5: 他們有一個宏大的計劃。
column6: Tāmen yǒu yī ge hóngdà de jìhuà.
column7: They have a grand plan.
column9: Grand in scale and ambition: 宏大的計劃, 宏大的規模, 宏大的場面. It is written and slightly formal, and it stresses grandeur rather than plain size: a building can be 宏大, but a big apple is just 大.

column3: Appears in labels and news: 特大暴雨 (a top-grade rainstorm), 特大号 (extra large), 特大城市 (a megacity). It is stronger than plain 大.
column4: 今天有特大暴雨。
column5: 今天有特大暴雨。
column6: Jīntiān yǒu tèdà bàoyǔ.
column7: There is a torrential rainstorm today.
column9: Appears in labels and news: 特大暴雨 (a top-grade rainstorm), 特大號 (extra large), 特大城市 (a megacity). It is stronger than plain 大.

column3: Besides measured length, it means a mishap in 万一有个长短 (if anything should happen), and 说长道短 is gossiping about people's good and bad points. 长 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.
column4: 这两根绳子长短不一样。
column5: 這兩根繩子長短不一樣。
column6: Zhè liǎng gēn shéngzi chángduǎn bù yīyàng.
column7: These two ropes are not the same length.
column9: Besides measured length, it means a mishap in 萬一有個長短 (if anything should happen), and 說長道短 is gossiping about people's good and bad points. 長 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.

column3: 通 adds “all the way through”, so the whole face, ears or iron is red: 脸通红, 冻得通红. It usually follows 得 after the cause: 羞得通红.
column4: 他的脸羞得通红。
column5: 他的臉羞得通紅。
column6: Tā de liǎn xiū de tōnghóng.
column7: His face turned bright red from embarrassment.
column9: 通 adds “all the way through”, so the whole face, ears or iron is red: 臉通紅, 凍得通紅. It usually follows 得 after the cause: 羞得通紅.

column3: Polite and formal: 行动不便 (limited mobility), 多有不便 (apologizing for the trouble), 不便透露 (not appropriate to disclose). In casual talk 不方便 is used.
column4: 老人行动不便。
column5: 老人行動不便。
column6: Lǎorén xíngdòng bùbiàn.
column7: The old man has trouble getting around.
column9: Polite and formal: 行動不便 (limited mobility), 多有不便 (apologizing for the trouble), 不便透露 (not appropriate to disclose). In casual talk 不方便 is used.

column3: Roads, pipes and noses can be 不通 (blocked). Writing or an argument that is 不通 makes no sense, and 行不通 says a plan will not work. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower; its meaning “no” came through 否, which was built on it.
column4: 这条路不通。
column5: 這條路不通。
column6: Zhè tiáo lù bùtōng.
column7: This road is blocked.
column9: Roads, pipes and noses can be 不通 (blocked). Writing or an argument that is 不通 makes no sense, and 行不通 says a plan will not work. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower; its meaning “no” came through 否, which was built on it.

column3: It is often used with 得 and a verb, as in 不值得去 (not worth going), and in set phrases: 不值钱 (worthless) and 不值一提 (not worth mentioning).
column4: 这点小事不值一提。
column5: 這點小事不值一提。
column6: Zhè diǎn xiǎo shì bùzhí yī tí.
column7: This small matter is not worth mentioning.
column9: It is often used with 得 and a verb, as in 不值得去 (not worth going), and in set phrases: 不值錢 (worthless) and 不值一提 (not worth mentioning).

column3: Softens a negative before a verb or adjective: 不怎么好 (not that good), 不怎么喜欢 (don't like it much). It does not ask how.
column4: 我不怎么喜欢吃辣。
column5: 我不怎麼喜歡吃辣。
column6: Wǒ bùzěnme xǐhuan chī là.
column7: I don't really like spicy food.
column9: Softens a negative before a verb or adjective: 不怎麼好 (not that good), 不怎麼喜歡 (don't like it much). It does not ask how.

column3: It stands at the end as a verdict: 这家餐厅不怎么样 (nothing special), a mild way to say poor. As an answer to “how was it?” it means so-so.
column4: 这部电影不怎么样。
column5: 這部電影不怎麼樣。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng bùzěnmeyàng.
column7: This movie is nothing special.
column9: It stands at the end as a verdict: 這家餐廳不怎麼樣 (nothing special), a mild way to say poor. As an answer to “how was it?” it means so-so.

column3: Followed by a verb: a feeling or action bursts out that you cannot stop, as in 不禁笑了, 不禁想起. It is more common in writing and storytelling than in plain speech.
column4: 听到这个消息，他不禁笑了。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他不禁笑了。
column6: Tīng dào zhè ge xiāoxi, tā bùjīn xiào le.
column7: Hearing the news, he could not help smiling.
column9: Followed by a verb: a feeling or action bursts out that you cannot stop, as in 不禁笑了, 不禁想起. It is more common in writing and storytelling than in plain speech.

column3: It opens the second clause of a story and turns it against what was planned or expected, usually for the worse: 本想…,不料…. Narrative and written style. 料 is rice 米 and a dipper 斗, a way of measuring or gauging.
column4: 我本想早点去,不料路上堵车了。
column5: 我本想早點去,不料路上塞車了。
column6: Wǒ běn xiǎng zǎodiǎn qù, bùliào lù shàng dǔchē le.
column7: I meant to go early, but unexpectedly there was a traffic jam.
column9: It opens the second clause of a story and turns it against what was planned or expected, usually for the worse: 本想…,不料…. Narrative and written style. 料 is rice 米 and a dipper 斗, a way of measuring or gauging.

column3: Says a result is unlikely to go that far, often to calm someone: 不至于吧 means surely it is not that bad. Without 不, 至于 asks whether it goes that far (至于吗?); 至于 also means as for.
column4: 你别担心,他不至于生气的。
column5: 你別擔心,他不至於生氣的。
column6: Nǐ bié dānxīn, tā bùzhìyú shēngqì de.
column7: Don't worry, he won't go so far as to get angry.
column9: Says a result is unlikely to go that far, often to calm someone: 不至於吧 means surely it is not that bad. Without 不, 至於 asks whether it goes that far (至於嗎?); 至於 also means as for.

column3: A stronger 不仅, with the point of going beyond a narrow view. It often appears as 不仅仅是 A,更是 B, or is followed by 而且, 还 or 也 to add more.
column4: 学汉语不仅仅是背单词。
column5: 學漢語不僅僅是背單詞。
column6: Xué Hànyǔ bùjǐnjǐn shì bèi dāncí.
column7: Learning Chinese is not just memorizing words.
column9: A stronger 不僅, with the point of going beyond a narrow view. It often appears as 不僅僅是 A,更是 B, or is followed by 而且, 還 or 也 to add more.

column3: Usually used as 与…无关 (has nothing to do with…). It also forms 无关紧要 (unimportant) and 无关人员, the people not involved, as on a notice.
column4: 这件事与你无关。
column5: 這件事與你無關。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yǔ nǐ wúguān.
column7: This matter has nothing to do with you.
column9: Usually used as 與…無關 (has nothing to do with…). It also forms 無關緊要 (unimportant) and 無關人員, the people not involved, as on a notice.

column3: Says that a ticket, vote, password or contract does not count, or that a medicine or measure does not work. In news, 抢救无效 reports that someone died despite emergency treatment.
column4: 这张票已经无效了。
column5: 這張票已經無效了。
column6: Zhè zhāng piào yǐjīng wúxiào le.
column7: This ticket is no longer valid.
column9: Says that a ticket, vote, password or contract does not count, or that a medicine or measure does not work. In news, 搶救無效 reports that someone died despite emergency treatment.

column3: Describes something whose edge cannot be seen: 无边无际 (boundless) or 无边的草原 (an endless grassland). It is a descriptive, somewhat literary word.
column4: 窗外是一片无边的草原。
column5: 窗外是一片無邊的草原。
column6: Chuāng wài shì yī piàn wúbiān de cǎoyuán.
column7: Outside the window is an endless grassland.
column9: Describes something whose edge cannot be seen: 無邊無際 (boundless) or 無邊的草原 (an endless grassland). It is a descriptive, somewhat literary word.

column3: A yes-or-no question made of 有 and 没有, so it does not take 吗. Before a noun it asks whether something exists; before a verb it asks whether something happened. Answer 有 or 没有.
column4: 你有没有带钥匙?
column5: 你有沒有帶鑰匙?
column6: Nǐ yǒuméiyǒu dài yàoshi?
column7: Did you bring the key?
column9: A yes-or-no question made of 有 and 沒有, so it does not take 嗎. Before a noun it asks whether something exists; before a verb it asks whether something happened. Answer 有 or 沒有.

column3: Fits good surprises as well as bad. Before a noun it takes 的: 意想不到的结果. Casual speech uses the shorter 想不到, as in 想不到你来了.
column4: 结果真是意想不到。
column5: 結果真是意想不到。
column6: Jiéguǒ zhēn shì yìxiǎngbùdào.
column7: The result is really unexpected.
column9: Fits good surprises as well as bad. Before a noun it takes 的: 意想不到的結果. Casual speech uses the shorter 想不到, as in 想不到你來了.

column3: Used for missing a bus, train or deadline (赶不上火车), or for not being able to keep up with a person or pace. The opposite is 赶得上, can still catch it.
column4: 快点,不然赶不上火车了。
column5: 快點,不然趕不上火車了。
column6: Kuài diǎn, bùrán gǎnbùshàng huǒchē le.
column7: Hurry, or we won't catch the train.
column9: Used for missing a bus, train or deadline (趕不上火車), or for not being able to keep up with a person or pace. The opposite is 趕得上, can still catch it.

column3: A pattern: verb + 得 + result means can, and 不 in place of 得 means cannot. So 看得见 pairs with 看不见, and likewise 听得见 and 听不见. 看 shows a hand 手 over an eye 目, as if shading the eyes to gaze far off.
column4: 你看得见黑板上的字吗?
column5: 你看得見黑板上的字嗎?
column6: Nǐ kàndejiàn hēibǎn shàng de zì ma?
column7: Can you see the writing on the blackboard?
column9: A pattern: verb + 得 + result means can, and 不 in place of 得 means cannot. So 看得見 pairs with 看不見, and likewise 聽得見 and 聽不見. 看 shows a hand 手 over an eye 目, as if shading the eyes to gaze far off.

column3: A formal, written version of 能不能, common in announcements, polite requests and essays: 能否借用…? Inside a sentence it also means whether: 能否成功取决于…. Speech says 能不能.
column4: 请问能否借用您的电话?
column5: 請問能否借用您的電話?
column6: Qǐngwèn néngfǒu jièyòng nín de diànhuà?
column7: May I borrow your phone, please?
column9: A formal, written version of 能不能, common in announcements, polite requests and essays: 能否借用…? Inside a sentence it also means whether: 能否成功取決於…. Speech says 能不能.

column3: A written word for spotting something far off: 远远望见, 望见灯塔. Everyday speech says 看见. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.
column4: 我们远远地望见了灯塔。
column5: 我們遠遠地望見了燈塔。
column6: Wǒmen yuǎnyuǎn de wàngjiàn le dēngtǎ.
column7: We spotted the lighthouse far away.
column9: A written word for spotting something far off: 遠遠望見, 望見燈塔. Everyday speech says 看見. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.

column3: An adverb that goes before the verb: 依次进入, 依次发言. It is the written-style choice; speech often says 按顺序 or 一个一个地.
column4: 请大家依次上车。
column5: 請大家依次上車。
column6: Qǐng dàjiā yīcì shàng chē.
column7: Everyone, please board one after another.
column9: An adverb that goes before the verb: 依次進入, 依次發言. It is the written-style choice; speech often says 按順序 or 一個一個地.

column3: Used for two things or people that look or are exactly alike, usually with 跟 or 和: 他跟他哥哥长得一模一样. In this word 模 is read mú and means a mold or pattern; it is also read mó, to imitate.
column4: 她和她妈妈长得一模一样。
column5: 她和她媽媽長得一模一樣。
column6: Tā hé tā māma zhǎng de yīmúyīyàng.
column7: She and her mother look exactly alike.
column9: Used for two things or people that look or are exactly alike, usually with 跟 or 和: 他跟他哥哥長得一模一樣. In this word 模 is read mú and means a mold or pattern; it is also read mó, to imitate.

column3: A literary word, rare on its own. You meet it in the set phrase 始终如一, unchanged from start to finish, said of a person's attitude or a habit that never wavers.
column4: 他对朋友始终如一。
column5: 他對朋友始終如一。
column6: Tā duì péngyou shǐzhōng rúyī.
column7: He has always been the same toward his friends.
column9: A literary word, rare on its own. You meet it in the set phrase 始終如一, unchanged from start to finish, said of a person's attitude or a habit that never wavers.

column3: Goes straight before a measure word and noun, with no 的: 同一个人, 同一时间, 同一所学校. It means one and the same thing, not two things that are alike (that is 一样).
column4: 我们住在同一栋楼。
column5: 我們住在同一棟樓。
column6: Wǒmen zhù zài tóngyī dòng lóu.
column7: We live in the same building.
column9: Goes straight before a measure word and noun, with no 的: 同一個人, 同一時間, 同一所學校. It means one and the same thing, not two things that are alike (that is 一樣).

column3: Before a noun it means disposable: 一次性筷子, 一次性杯子. As a modifier of a verb it means in one go: 一次性付款, 一次性解决. For disposable chopsticks and tableware the mainland says 一次性, while Taiwan says 免洗筷 and 免洗餐具.
column4: 这家餐厅提供一次性筷子。
column5: 這家餐廳提供一次性筷子。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng tígōng yīcìxìng kuàizi.
column7: This restaurant provides disposable chopsticks.
column9: Before a noun it means disposable: 一次性筷子, 一次性杯子. As a modifier of a verb it means in one go: 一次性付款, 一次性解決. For disposable chopsticks and tableware the mainland says 一次性, while Taiwan says 免洗筷 and 免洗餐具.

column3: Usually doubled: 时而…时而… sets two states side by side that alternate, “now this, now that”. It can also stand alone before one verb for “once in a while”.
column4: 天气时而晴,时而阴。
column5: 天氣時而晴,時而陰。
column6: Tiānqì shí'ér qíng, shí'ér yīn.
column7: The weather is sometimes sunny, sometimes cloudy.
column9: Usually doubled: 時而…時而… sets two states side by side that alternate, “now this, now that”. It can also stand alone before one verb for “once in a while”.

column3: Said of something about to happen, usually with 就要, 就 or 要: 眼看天就要黑了. It can also mean watching something bad happen without being able to stop it.
column4: 眼看天就要黑了,我们快走吧。
column5: 眼看天就要黑了,我們快走吧。
column6: Yǎnkàn tiān jiù yào hēi le, wǒmen kuài zǒu ba.
column7: It's about to get dark; let's hurry.
column9: Said of something about to happen, usually with 就要, 就 or 要: 眼看天就要黑了. It can also mean watching something bad happen without being able to stop it.

column3: A formal, written “will surely”, for confident statements about the future in news, speeches and slogans. In conversation people say 一定会 instead.
column4: 坚持努力,你必将成功。
column5: 堅持努力,你必將成功。
column6: Jiānchí nǔlì, nǐ bìjiāng chénggōng.
column7: Keep working hard and you will surely succeed.
column9: A formal, written “will surely”, for confident statements about the future in news, speeches and slogans. In conversation people say 一定會 instead.

column3: Looks back from a moment just mentioned: “before this”, “until then”. Mostly written, in news and reports; its mirror word is 此后. 此 pictures where a person stops, which gives “here”.
column4: 此前他从没来过这里。
column5: 此前他從沒來過這裡。
column6: Cǐqián tā cóng méi lái guo zhèlǐ.
column7: He had never been here before this.
column9: Looks back from a moment just mentioned: “before this”, “until then”. Mostly written, in news and reports; its mirror word is 此後. 此 pictures where a person stops, which gives “here”.

column3: Looks back once something is over: afterwards, in hindsight. It is behind the saying 事后诸葛亮, a “Zhuge Liang after the event” who is wise only in hindsight. The opposite is 事前.
column4: 事后他才发现自己错了。
column5: 事後他才發現自己錯了。
column6: Shìhòu tā cái fāxiàn zìjǐ cuò le.
column7: Only afterwards did he realize he had been wrong.
column9: Looks back once something is over: afterwards, in hindsight. It is behind the saying 事後諸葛亮, a “Zhuge Liang after the event” who is wise only in hindsight. The opposite is 事前. The older form of 後 showed in oracle bone script a foot bound by a rope, so it lagged behind.

column3: Used alone it means “later, once this is over”, as in 过后再说, “let's deal with it later”. After a time word or event it means “after that”: 雨过后, “after the rain”.
column4: 这件事过后再说吧。
column5: 這件事過後再說吧。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì guòhòu zài shuō ba.
column7: Let's deal with this later.
column9: Used alone it means “later, once this is over”, as in 過後再說, “let's deal with it later”. After a time word or event it means “after that”: 雨過後, “after the rain”.

column3: Looks ahead in time from now: “from here on”, while 以后 can also mean “after” an event. It is also plain direction, backward, as in 往后退, “step back”.
column4: 往后的日子会越来越好。
column5: 往後的日子會越來越好。
column6: Wǎnghòu de rìzi huì yuè lái yuè hǎo.
column7: The days ahead will get better and better.
column9: Looks ahead in time from now: “from here on”, while 以後 can also mean “after” an event. It is also plain direction, backward, as in 往後退, “step back”.

column3: “This issue” or “this period” for a magazine, a TV series, a course or a financial report, with 上期 for the last one and 下期 for the next. 期 has a Taiwan reading, qí.
column4: 本期节目到此结束。
column5: 本期節目到此結束。
column6: Běnqī jiémù dào cǐ jiéshù.
column7: This episode of the program ends here.
column9: “This issue” or “this period” for a magazine, a TV series, a course or a financial report, with 上期 for the last one and 下期 for the next. 期 has a Taiwan reading, qí.

column3: Most often the same stretch of an earlier year, in reports and news: 与去年同期相比, “compared with the same period last year”. It can also mean happening at the same time. 期 has a Taiwan reading, qí.
column4: 今年的销量比去年同期增长了一成。
column5: 今年的銷量比去年同期增長了一成。
column6: Jīnnián de xiāoliàng bǐ qùnián tóngqī zēngzhǎng le yī chéng.
column7: This year's sales are up ten percent over the same period last year.
column9: Most often the same stretch of an earlier year, in reports and news: 與去年同期相比, “compared with the same period last year”. It can also mean happening at the same time. 期 has a Taiwan reading, qí.

column3: Looks far ahead in time, and goes before words like 打算, 利益 and 发展. It is the opposite of 眼前, what is right in front of you. 长 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.
column4: 做事要看得长远一点。
column5: 做事要看得長遠一點。
column6: Zuò shì yào kàn de chángyuǎn yīdiǎn.
column7: You should look further ahead when you do things.
column9: Looks far ahead in time, and goes before words like 打算, 利益 and 發展. It is the opposite of 眼前, what is right in front of you. 長 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.

column3: Out of date: fashions, ideas, technology and slang that are no longer current. Less often it means being past a stated or agreed time.
column4: 这种手机已经过时了。
column5: 這種手機已經過時了。
column6: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī yǐjīng guòshí le.
column7: This kind of phone is already out of date.
column9: Out of date: fashions, ideas, technology and slang that are no longer current. Less often it means being past a stated or agreed time.

column3: A noun for the opening part of a story, speech, letter or text: 故事的开头. Unlike 开始, which marks the moment something starts, it names the first stretch itself, as in 开头难, “the start is the hardest”.
column4: 这个故事的开头很有意思。
column5: 這個故事的開頭很有意思。
column6: Zhège gùshi de kāitóu hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: The beginning of this story is very interesting.
column9: A noun for the opening part of a story, speech, letter or text: 故事的開頭. Unlike 開始, which marks the moment something starts, it names the first stretch itself, as in 開頭難, “the start is the hardest”.

column3: The place where a race, trip or route starts; also a person's starting level in life or work. Its opposite is 终点, the finish.
column4: 马拉松的起点就在这个广场。
column5: 馬拉松的起點就在這個廣場。
column6: Mǎlāsōng de qǐdiǎn jiù zài zhège guǎngchǎng.
column7: The marathon starts right in this square.
column9: The place where a race, trip or route starts; also a person's starting level in life or work. Its opposite is 終點, the finish.

column3: Works as an adjective before a noun (最终结果) or as an adverb before a verb: after everything, in the end. It suggests a long process came to a result. 终 began as a picture of the knot at the end of a cord.
column4: 最终他还是同意了。
column5: 最終他還是同意了。
column6: Zuìzhōng tā háishi tóngyì le.
column7: In the end he agreed anyway.
column9: Works as an adjective before a noun (最終結果) or as an adverb before a verb: after everything, in the end. It suggests a long process came to a result. 終 began as a picture of the knot at the end of a cord.

column3: A cutoff point in news and reports: “as of” a date or moment, with the count so far following. Common are 截至目前 and 截至昨天.
column4: 截至昨天,已有三百人报名。
column5: 截至昨天,已有三百人報名。
column6: Jiézhì zuótiān, yǐ yǒu sānbǎi rén bàomíng.
column7: As of yesterday, 300 people have signed up.
column9: A cutoff point in news and reports: “as of” a date or moment, with the count so far following. Common are 截至目前 and 截至昨天.

column3: Done at a set time or at regular times: 定时吃药, “take medicine on schedule”. Also a timer setting, as in 定时炸弹, “time bomb”, and 定时器.
column4: 你要定时吃药。
column5: 你要定時吃藥。
column6: Nǐ yào dìngshí chī yào.
column7: You need to take your medicine on schedule.
column9: Done at a set time or at regular times: 定時吃藥, “take medicine on schedule”. Also a timer setting, as in 定時炸彈, “time bomb”, and 定時器.

column3: “For the first time”, placed before a verb. A news and written word: in speech people usually say 第一次.
column4: 他首次来到中国。
column5: 他首次來到中國。
column6: Tā shǒucì láidào Zhōngguó.
column7: He came to China for the first time.
column9: “For the first time”, placed before a verb. A news and written word: in speech people usually say 第一次.

column3: “This time”, for the event under discussion: 此次会议, 此次活动. Formal and written; in speech people say 这次.
column4: 此次会议很成功。
column5: 此次會議很成功。
column6: Cǐcì huìyì hěn chénggōng.
column7: This meeting was a great success.
column9: “This time”, for the event under discussion: 此次會議, 此次活動. Formal and written; in speech people say 這次.

column3: “This matter”, pointing back to something just mentioned. Formal and written, as in 此事与你无关; in speech people say 这件事.
column4: 此事与你无关。
column5: 此事與你無關。
column6: Cǐshì yǔ nǐ wúguān.
column7: This has nothing to do with you.
column9: “This matter”, pointing back to something just mentioned. Formal and written, as in 此事與你無關; in speech people say 這件事.

column3: To send out or turn out in force: police, firefighters, troops, rescue teams. 全体出动 means everyone goes out.
column4: 消防车立刻出动了。
column5: 消防車立刻出動了。
column6: Xiāofángchē lìkè chūdòng le.
column7: The fire trucks set out right away.
column9: To send out or turn out in force: police, firefighters, troops, rescue teams. 全體出動 means everyone goes out.

column3: A way out of a trap or difficulty, and so a future: 没有出路 means hopeless. It also covers career prospects and the outlet for a product. 出 pictures a foot stepping out of a cave, so “exit”.
column4: 年轻人要为自己找出路。
column5: 年輕人要為自己找出路。
column6: Niánqīngrén yào wèi zìjǐ zhǎo chūlù.
column7: Young people have to find their own way forward.
column9: A way out of a trap or difficulty, and so a future: 沒有出路 means hopeless. It also covers career prospects and the outlet for a product. 出 pictures a foot stepping out of a cave, so “exit”.

column3: To step in personally, in one's own name, usually someone with standing: 出面解决, 出面道歉. Unlike 出现, it is not just to appear.
column4: 这件事得由经理出面解决。
column5: 這件事得由經理出面解決。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì děi yóu jīnglǐ chūmiàn jiějué.
column7: The manager has to step in and settle this.
column9: To step in personally, in one's own name, usually someone with standing: 出面解決, 出面道歉. Unlike 出現, it is not just to appear.

column3: Two senses: going in and out (出入口, a doorway), and a mismatch between figures or accounts: 数字有出入, “the numbers don't match”. 入 is an arrowhead pointing in, for “to enter”.
column4: 两份报告的数字有出入。
column5: 兩份報告的數字有出入。
column6: Liǎng fèn bàogào de shùzì yǒu chūrù.
column7: The figures in the two reports don't match.
column9: Two senses: going in and out (出入口, a doorway), and a mismatch between figures or accounts: 數字有出入, “the numbers don't match”. 入 is an arrowhead pointing in, for “to enter”.

column3: To roll out a policy, rule or measure: 新规出台, “the new rules are issued”. It is a news word for officials. It can also mean to step onto a stage.
column4: 政府出台了新的规定。
column5: 政府出臺了新的規定。
column6: Zhèngfǔ chūtái le xīn de guīdìng.
column7: The government issued new rules.
column9: To roll out a policy, rule or measure: 新規出臺, “the new rules are issued”. It is a news word for officials. It can also mean to step onto a stage.

column3: To launch or release something to the public: a product, a program, a new model: 推出新产品. The plain push-out sense also exists, but the launch sense is the usual one.
column4: 公司推出了一款新手机。
column5: 公司推出了一款新手機。
column6: Gōngsī tuīchū le yī kuǎn xīn shǒujī.
column7: The company launched a new phone.
column9: To launch or release something to the public: a product, a program, a new model: 推出新產品. The plain push-out sense also exists, but the launch sense is the usual one.

column3: Used for sending people on a task: police officers, troops, a delegation, a representative. The local police station is 派出所. Besides "to send," 派 also means a faction or school, as in 学派 and 党派.
column4: 公司派出两个人去北京出差。
column5: 公司派出兩個人去北京出差。
column6: Gōngsī pàichū liǎng gè rén qù Běijīng chūchāi.
column7: The company is sending two people to Beijing on a business trip.
column9: Used for sending people on a task: police officers, troops, a delegation, a representative. The local police station is 派出所. Besides "to send," 派 also means a faction or school, as in 學派 and 黨派.

column3: The 出 after a verb marks a result: 查 means to check, 查出 means the checking turned something up. The same pattern gives 看出, 找出 and 听出.
column4: 医生查出了问题的原因。
column5: 醫生查出了問題的原因。
column6: Yīshēng cháchū le wèntí de yuányīn.
column7: The doctor found the cause of the problem.
column9: The 出 after a verb marks a result: 查 means to check, 查出 means the checking turned something up. The same pattern gives 看出, 找出 and 聽出.

column3: Said of a performer, player or speaker stepping onto the stage or field; the opposite is 退场. A fee for appearing is 出场费.
column4: 主角在第二幕才出场。
column5: 主角在第二幕才出場。
column6: Zhǔjué zài dì èr mù cái chūchǎng.
column7: The lead does not come on until the second act.
column9: Said of a performer, player or speaker stepping onto the stage or field; the opposite is 退場. A fee for appearing is 出場費.

column3: A news and diplomatic word for a leader or official going abroad on an official visit; for an ordinary trip you would just say 去.
column4: 总理明天将出访三个国家。
column5: 總理明天將出訪三個國家。
column6: Zǒnglǐ míngtiān jiāng chūfǎng sān gè guójiā.
column7: The premier will visit three countries starting tomorrow.
column9: A news and diplomatic word for a leader or official going abroad on an official visit; for an ordinary trip you would just say 去.

column3: More formal and more abstract than plain 藏: it fits hidden files, hidden dangers, feelings or identities kept out of sight.
column4: 他一直隐藏着自己的真实身份。
column5: 他一直隱藏著自己的真實身分。
column6: Tā yīzhí yǐncáng zhe zìjǐ de zhēnshí shēnfèn.
column7: He has always hidden his true identity.
column9: More formal and more abstract than plain 藏: it fits hidden files, hidden dangers, feelings or identities kept out of sight.

column3: It goes with 保护 (protect), 侵犯 (invade) and 泄露 (leak): 保护隐私, 个人隐私. Phone and internet privacy settings use this word.
column4: 请保护好你的个人隐私。
column5: 請保護好你的個人隱私。
column6: Qǐng bǎohù hǎo nǐ de gèrén yǐnsī.
column7: Please protect your personal privacy.
column9: It goes with 保護 (protect), 侵犯 (invade) and 泄露 (leak): 保護隱私, 個人隱私. Phone and internet privacy settings use this word.

column3: Often something you wanted kept secret or covered: 暴露身份, 暴露目标, or skin left bare to the sun. A weak spot, mistake or secret gets 暴露. Besides "violent," 暴 can mean to expose to the sun.
column4: 他的口音暴露了他是外地人。
column5: 他的口音暴露了他是外地人。
column6: Tā de kǒuyīn bàolù le tā shì wàidì rén.
column7: His accent gave away that he is from out of town.
column9: Often something you wanted kept secret or covered: 暴露身分, 暴露目標, or skin left bare to the sun. A weak spot, mistake or secret gets 暴露. Besides "violent," 暴 can mean to expose to the sun.

column3: Found in spoken words for showing up or giving something away: 露面 (put in an appearance), 露馅 (let the secret out), 露一手 (show off a skill).
column4: 她不小心露了馅。
column5: 她不小心露了餡。
column6: Tā bù xiǎoxīn lòu le xiàn.
column7: She accidentally let the secret out.
column9: Found in spoken words for showing up or giving something away: 露面 (put in an appearance), 露餡 (let the secret out), 露一手 (show off a skill).

column3: What shows is usually a quality or feeling that comes out on its own: 显出疲惫, 显出才华. To say something looks a certain way, 显得 is far more common.
column4: 她脸上显出一丝疲惫。
column5: 她臉上顯出一絲疲憊。
column6: Tā liǎn shang xiǎnchū yī sī píbèi.
column7: A trace of tiredness showed on her face.
column9: What shows is usually a quality or feeling that comes out on its own: 顯出疲憊, 顯出才華. To say something looks a certain way, 顯得 is far more common.

column3: What gets told is information: news, plans, a name, or a feeling that slips out (透露出一丝不满). Unlike 暴露, it is often done on purpose, to a few people.
column4: 他没有透露自己的计划。
column5: 他沒有透露自己的計劃。
column6: Tā méiyǒu tòulù zìjǐ de jìhuà.
column7: He did not reveal his plans.
column9: What gets told is information: news, plans, a name, or a feeling that slips out (透露出一絲不滿). Unlike 暴露, it is often done on purpose, to a few people.

column3: Mostly seen inside longer words: 揭开 (lift off a lid or cover), 揭露 (expose wrongdoing), 揭晓 (announce results), 揭穿 (see through a lie).
column4: 他把墙上的海报揭了。
column5: 他把牆上的海報揭了。
column6: Tā bǎ qiáng shang de hǎibào jiē le.
column7: He peeled the poster off the wall.
column9: Mostly seen inside longer words: 揭開 (lift off a lid or cover), 揭露 (expose wrongdoing), 揭曉 (announce results), 揭穿 (see through a lie).

column3: The shadow an object casts, but also a lasting bad impression: 心理阴影 or 童年阴影 is a psychological scar. The everyday word for your own shadow is 影子.
column4: 树的阴影落在地上。
column5: 樹的陰影落在地上。
column6: Shù de yīnyǐng luò zài dì shang.
column7: The tree's shadow falls on the ground.
column9: The shadow an object casts, but also a lasting bad impression: 心理陰影 or 童年陰影 is a psychological scar. The everyday word for your own shadow is 影子.

column3: In speech it means to fool someone (蒙人), to guess blindly (蒙对), or to be dazed (被打蒙了).
column4: 这道题我是蒙的，没想到蒙对了。
column5: 這道題我是蒙的，沒想到蒙對了。
column6: Zhè dào tí wǒ shì mēng de, méi xiǎngdào mēng duì le.
column7: I just guessed this question, and I guessed right.
column9: In speech it means to fool someone (蒙人), to guess blindly (蒙對), or to be dazed (被打蒙了).

column3: Always a secret and harmful scheme, unlike the neutral 计划. Set phrases: 阴谋诡计 (dirty tricks), 阴谋论 (conspiracy theory). 阴 also means hidden, which fits a plot kept in the dark.
column4: 他们的阴谋被警察发现了。
column5: 他們的陰謀被警察發現了。
column6: Tāmen de yīnmóu bèi jǐngchá fāxiàn le.
column7: Their plot was discovered by the police.
column9: Always a secret and harmful scheme, unlike the neutral 計劃. Set phrases: 陰謀詭計 (dirty tricks), 陰謀論 (conspiracy theory). 陰 also means hidden, which fits a plot kept in the dark.

column3: For things that go well together: clothes, colors, foods. In language study, 词语搭配 means which words normally go with which, collocations.
column4: 这条围巾和你的外套很搭配。
column5: 這條圍巾和你的外套很搭配。
column6: Zhè tiáo wéijīn hé nǐ de wàitào hěn dāpèi.
column7: This scarf goes well with your coat.
column9: For things that go well together: clothes, colors, foods. In language study, 詞語搭配 means which words normally go with which, collocations.

column3: A partner in a pair doing a job together: a comedy duo, police partners, a doubles team. It is also a verb: 我想和你搭档. In Taiwan, the dàng reading of 档 is read dǎng instead, so the word is dādǎng there.
column4: 他们是多年的搭档。
column5: 他們是多年的搭檔。
column6: Tāmen shì duō nián de dādàng.
column7: They have been partners for many years.
column9: A partner in a pair doing a job together: a comedy duo, police partners, a doubles team. It is also a verb: 我想和你搭檔. In Taiwan, the dàng reading of 檔 is read dǎng instead, so the word is dādǎng there.

column3: Mostly for abstract things coming together into something new: cultures, styles, technologies, ethnic groups (文化融合). 融 ran from heat, to melting, to blending, as things melt into one.
column4: 这家餐厅把中餐和西餐融合在一起。
column5: 這家餐廳把中餐和西餐融合在一起。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng bǎ zhōngcān hé xīcān rónghé zài yīqǐ.
column7: This restaurant blends Chinese and Western cooking.
column9: Mostly for abstract things coming together into something new: cultures, styles, technologies, ethnic groups (文化融合). 融 ran from heat, to melting, to blending, as things melt into one.

column3: One thing melts into another, usually a person into a group or place: 融入社会, 融入新环境. Compare 融合, where two things merge with each other. 入 is an arrowhead indicating entering.
column4: 他很快就融入了新班级。
column5: 他很快就融入了新班級。
column6: Tā hěn kuài jiù róngrù le xīn bānjí.
column7: He soon fit into his new class.
column9: One thing melts into another, usually a person into a group or place: 融入社會, 融入新環境. Compare 融合, where two things merge with each other. 入 is an arrowhead indicating entering.

column3: Describes relationships, atmospheres, colors and sounds that fit together; 和谐社会 (harmonious society) was a mainland government slogan. Online, 被和谐 means a post got censored.
column4: 他们一家人相处得很和谐。
column5: 他們一家人相處得很和諧。
column6: Tāmen yī jiā rén xiāngchǔ de hěn héxié.
column7: Their family gets along very harmoniously.
column9: Describes relationships, atmospheres, colors and sounds that fit together; 和諧社會 (harmonious society) was a mainland government slogan. Online, 被和諧 means a post got censored.

column3: Mostly figurative: companies, countries or teams joining forces toward a goal, usually followed by a verb, as in 联手打造 (jointly create) or 联手对付.
column4: 两家公司联手推出了新产品。
column5: 兩家公司聯手推出了新產品。
column6: Liǎng jiā gōngsī liánshǒu tuīchū le xīn chǎnpǐn.
column7: The two companies teamed up to launch a new product.
column9: Mostly figurative: companies, countries or teams joining forces toward a goal, usually followed by a verb, as in 聯手打造 (jointly create) or 聯手對付.

column3: Physically getting what is sent or handed over: a signal, an email, goods, or taking over an organization. Accepting a gift or idea is 接受 (jiēshòu).
column4: 我已经接收到你的邮件了。
column5: 我已經接收到你的郵件了。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng jiēshōu dào nǐ de yóujiàn le.
column7: I have received your email.
column9: Physically getting what is sent or handed over: a signal, an email, goods, or taking over an organization. Accepting a gift or idea is 接受 (jiēshòu).

column3: Collecting what is due: fees, rent, deposits (收取费用, 收取押金). The party doing the charging is the subject; picking up your own package is 领取 or 取. 取 shows an ear and a hand: it recalls a hunters' rite of taking the ear of fallen prey.
column4: 银行会收取一定的手续费。
column5: 銀行會收取一定的手續費。
column6: Yínháng huì shōuqǔ yīdìng de shǒuxùfèi.
column7: The bank charges a certain fee.
column9: Collecting what is due: fees, rent, deposits (收取費用, 收取押金). The party doing the charging is the subject; picking up your own package is 領取 or 取. 取 shows an ear and a hand: it recalls a hunters' rite of taking the ear of fallen prey.

column3: Taking in someone else's child or a stray animal and raising it as your own: 收养孩子, 收养流浪猫. For keeping your own pet, plain 养 is enough.
column4: 他们收养了一只流浪狗。
column5: 他們收養了一隻流浪狗。
column6: Tāmen shōuyǎng le yī zhī liúlàng gǒu.
column7: They adopted a stray dog.
column9: Taking in someone else's child or a stray animal and raising it as your own: 收養孩子, 收養流浪貓. For keeping your own pet, plain 養 is enough.

column3: Collecting as a hobby (stamps, art, antiques), or keeping something safe. On apps and sites, 收藏 is also the button that saves a page or item to favorites.
column4: 他收藏了很多老邮票。
column5: 他收藏了很多老郵票。
column6: Tā shōucáng le hěn duō lǎo yóupiào.
column7: He has collected a lot of old stamps.
column9: Collecting as a hobby (stamps, art, antiques), or keeping something safe. On apps and sites, 收藏 is also the button that saves a page or item to favorites.

column3: For collecting what is yours by right, usually at a counter or office after showing proof: 领取奖金, 领取包裹, 领取护照.
column4: 请凭号码领取你的行李。
column5: 請憑號碼領取你的行李。
column6: Qǐng píng hàomǎ lǐngqǔ nǐ de xíngli.
column7: Please claim your luggage with your number.
column9: For collecting what is yours by right, usually at a counter or office after showing proof: 領取獎金, 領取包裹, 領取護照.

column3: It means watching over someone or something so that it stays put and safe: 看管孩子, 看管行李, 看管犯人.
column4: 请你帮我看管一下行李。
column5: 請你幫我看管一下行李。
column6: Qǐng nǐ bāng wǒ kānguǎn yī xià xíngli.
column7: Please keep an eye on my luggage for a moment.
column9: It means watching over someone or something so that it stays put and safe: 看管孩子, 看管行李, 看管犯人.

column3: It rarely stands alone: it works in compounds such as 保护, 爱护 and 护士.
column4: 我们要保护环境。
column5: 我們要保護環境。
column6: Wǒmen yào bǎo hù huánjìng.
column7: We must protect the environment.
column9: It rarely stands alone: it works in compounds such as 保護, 愛護 and 護士.

column3: Here it is about keeping watch over a person, a place or a thing: 看门, 看孩子.
column4: 他在家看孩子。
column5: 他在家看孩子。
column6: Tā zài jiā kān háizi.
column7: He stays home to look after the kids.
column9: Here it is about keeping watch over a person, a place or a thing: 看門, 看孩子.

column3: A formal word for holding documents, shares or views: 持有护照, 持有股票, 持有不同意见.
column4: 他持有美国护照。
column5: 他持有美國護照。
column6: Tā chíyǒu Měiguó hùzhào.
column7: He holds an American passport.
column9: A formal word for holding documents, shares or views: 持有護照, 持有股票, 持有不同意見.

column3: Used for gifts to an institution or a cause, such as books, money or organs: 捐赠图书, 器官捐赠.
column4: 他把藏书捐赠给了图书馆。
column5: 他把藏書捐贈給了圖書館。
column6: Tā bǎ cángshū juānzèng gěi le túshūguǎn.
column7: He donated his book collection to the library.
column9: Used for gifts to an institution or a cause, such as books, money or organs: 捐贈圖書, 器官捐贈.

column3: Giving money or goods to help people in need, as in 捐助灾区 or 捐助贫困学生.
column4: 很多人为灾区捐助了钱和物。
column5: 很多人為災區捐助了錢和物。
column6: Hěn duō rén wèi zāiqū juānzhù le qián hé wù.
column7: Many people donated money and goods to the disaster area.
column9: Giving money or goods to help people in need, as in 捐助災區 or 捐助貧困學生.

column3: Help for people or animals in trouble, often given by an organization: 救助站, 救助流浪动物.
column4: 志愿者救助了很多流浪狗。
column5: 志願者救助了很多流浪狗。
column6: Zhìyuànzhě jiùzhù le hěn duō liúlàng gǒu.
column7: Volunteers rescued many stray dogs.
column9: Help for people or animals in trouble, often given by an organization: 救助站, 救助流浪動物.

column3: Rescue work in an emergency, done by teams that arrive from outside: 救援队, 救援人员, 救援行动.
column4: 救援人员很快赶到了现场。
column5: 救援人員很快趕到了現場。
column6: Jiùyuán rényuán hěn kuài gǎndào le xiànchǎng.
column7: The rescue workers soon reached the scene.
column9: Rescue work in an emergency, done by teams that arrive from outside: 救援隊, 救援人員, 救援行動.

column3: Aid from a government, an organization or a country: 经济援助, 医疗援助, 对外援助.
column4: 该国向灾区提供了医疗援助。
column5: 該國向災區提供了醫療援助。
column6: Gāi guó xiàng zāiqū tígōng le yīliáo yuánzhù.
column7: That country provided medical aid to the disaster area.
column9: Aid from a government, an organization or a country: 經濟援助, 醫療援助, 對外援助.

column3: A formal, written word whose objects are usually abstract: 给予帮助, 给予支持, 给予关心. In this word 给 has its bound reading, meaning to supply or provide.
column4: 老师给予了我很大的帮助。
column5: 老師給予了我很大的幫助。
column6: Lǎoshī jǐyǔ le wǒ hěn dà de bāngzhù.
column7: My teacher gave me a lot of help.
column9: A formal, written word whose objects are usually abstract: 給予幫助, 給予支持, 給予關心. In this word 給 has its bound reading, meaning to supply or provide.

column3: Mostly a term for supply, in economics and in utilities: 供给和需求, 电力供给. Here 给 has its bound reading, meaning to supply or provide.
column4: 市场上的供给超过了需求。
column5: 市場上的供給超過了需求。
column6: Shìchǎng shàng de gōngjǐ chāoguò le xūqiú.
column7: The supply on the market exceeded demand.
column9: Mostly a term for supply, in economics and in utilities: 供給和需求, 電力供給. Here 給 has its bound reading, meaning to supply or provide.

column3: Praise for giving one's time, effort or life to a cause or to others: 无私奉献, 奉献青春.
column4: 他一生都在为教育事业奉献。
column5: 他一生都在為教育事業奉獻。
column6: Tā yīshēng dōu zài wèi jiàoyù shìyè fèngxiàn.
column7: He devoted his whole life to education.
column9: Praise for giving one's time, effort or life to a cause or to others: 無私奉獻, 奉獻青春.

column3: An official handing out of money or goods to many people, by a company or government: 发放工资, 发放补贴.
column4: 公司每月十号发放工资。
column5: 公司每月十號發放工資。
column6: Gōngsī měi yuè shí hào fāfàng gōngzī.
column7: The company pays salaries on the tenth of every month.
column9: An official handing out of money or goods to many people, by a company or government: 發放工資, 發放補貼.

column3: Often carries a note of worry about relying too much: 依赖手机, 过分依赖, and the noun use 对父母的依赖.
column4: 现在很多人太依赖手机了。
column5: 現在很多人太依賴手機了。
column6: Xiànzài hěn duō rén tài yīlài shǒujī le.
column7: Nowadays many people depend too much on their phones.
column9: Often carries a note of worry about relying too much: 依賴手機, 過分依賴, and the noun use 對父母的依賴.

column3: In speech it means to blame (都赖你, 别赖我) and turns up in 不赖, "not bad". It also means to stay put (赖床) or to deny (赖账).
column4: 这都赖你，你为什么不早说？
column5: 這都賴你，你為什麼不早說？
column6: Zhè dōu lài nǐ, nǐ wèishénme bù zǎo shuō?
column7: This is all your fault; why didn't you say so earlier?
column9: In speech it means to blame (都賴你, 別賴我) and turns up in 不賴, "not bad". It also means to stay put (賴床) or to deny (賴帳).

column3: Used for physical props and for keeping something going: 支撑屋顶, 支撑家庭, and 支撑不住 for being unable to hold out.
column4: 这根柱子支撑着整个屋顶。
column5: 這根柱子支撐著整個屋頂。
column6: Zhè gēn zhùzi zhīchēng zhe zhěnggè wūdǐng.
column7: This pillar holds up the whole roof.
column9: Used for physical props and for keeping something going: 支撐屋頂, 支撐家庭, and 支撐不住 for being unable to hold out.

column3: Switching one thing for another among possibilities, with no sense of getting better: 变换位置, 变换角度, 变换颜色.
column4: 他不停地变换姿势。
column5: 他不停地變換姿勢。
column6: Tā bù tíng de biànhuàn zīshì.
column7: He keeps changing his posture.
column9: Switching one thing for another among possibilities, with no sense of getting better: 變換位置, 變換角度, 變換顏色.

column3: A positive word for replacing old methods or systems with new ones: 技术革新, 革新者.
column4: 这家公司不断进行技术革新。
column5: 這家公司不斷進行技術革新。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī bùduàn jìnxíng jìshù géxīn.
column7: This company keeps innovating its technology.
column9: A positive word for replacing old methods or systems with new ones: 技術革新, 革新者.

column3: Something spins around an axis by itself: 车轮转动, 风车转动, 地球转动. The spinning thing is usually the subject of the sentence, not an object someone turns.
column4: 风车在风中慢慢转动。
column5: 風車在風中慢慢轉動。
column6: Fēngchē zài fēng zhōng mànmàn zhuàndòng.
column7: The windmill turns slowly in the wind.
column9: Something spins around an axis by itself: 車輪轉動, 風車轉動, 地球轉動. The spinning thing is usually the subject of the sentence, not an object someone turns.

column3: Spinning around a center, often continuously: 旋转门, 旋转木马, 地球旋转. For a knob or key that is simply turned by hand, 转动 is the more usual word.
column4: 地球一直在旋转。
column5: 地球一直在旋轉。
column6: Dìqiú yīzhí zài xuánzhuǎn.
column7: The earth is always spinning.
column9: Spinning around a center, often continuously: 旋轉門, 旋轉木馬, 地球旋轉. For a knob or key that is simply turned by hand, 轉動 is the more usual word.

column3: Used for something that was bad and is getting better, such as an illness or a situation: 病情好转, 经济好转.
column4: 他的病情已经好转了。
column5: 他的病情已經好轉了。
column6: Tā de bìngqíng yǐjīng hǎozhuǎn le.
column7: His condition has already improved.
column9: Used for something that was bad and is getting better, such as an illness or a situation: 病情好轉, 經濟好轉.

column3: Used for raising something abstract, such as quality, skill or efficiency (提升能力), and for being promoted at work.
column4: 这门课帮我提升了英语水平。
column5: 這門課幫我提升了英語水平。
column6: Zhè mén kè bāng wǒ tíshēng le Yīngyǔ shuǐpíng.
column7: This course helped me improve my English.
column9: Used for raising something abstract, such as quality, skill or efficiency (提升能力), and for being promoted at work.

column3: Added to a word, 化 makes a process of becoming, as in 绿化 and 现代化. 深化 is for abstract things such as reform and cooperation.
column4: 两国决定进一步深化合作。
column5: 兩國決定進一步深化合作。
column6: Liǎng guó juédìng jìn yī bù shēnhuà hézuò.
column7: The two countries decided to deepen their cooperation further.
column9: Added to a word, 化 makes a process of becoming, as in 綠化 and 現代化. 深化 is for abstract things such as reform and cooperation.

column3: 化 after a noun or adjective makes a verb meaning to make or become that way (绿化, 美化, 现代化). 强化 goes with abstract objects such as 管理, 意识 and 监督.
column4: 我们要强化安全意识。
column5: 我們要強化安全意識。
column6: Wǒmen yào qiánghuà ānquán yìshí.
column7: We need to strengthen safety awareness.
column9: 化 after a noun or adjective makes a verb meaning to make or become that way (綠化, 美化, 現代化). 強化 goes with abstract objects such as 管理, 意識 and 監督.

column3: It takes abstract objects: 巩固基础, 巩固成果, and for study, 巩固知识, meaning to make what you learned stick through practice. It also works as an adjective: 地位很巩固.
column4: 复习可以巩固所学的知识。
column5: 複習可以鞏固所學的知識。
column6: Fùxí kěyǐ gǒnggù suǒ xué de zhīshì.
column7: Review helps consolidate what you have learned.
column9: It takes abstract objects: 鞏固基礎, 鞏固成果, and for study, 鞏固知識, meaning to make what you learned stick through practice. It also works as an adjective: 地位很鞏固.

column3: It goes with things that grow between people or in the body: 增进友谊, 增进了解, 增进健康. For plain amounts and numbers, such as 人数 or 收入, use 增加 instead.
column4: 旅行可以增进朋友之间的感情。
column5: 旅行可以增進朋友之間的感情。
column6: Lǚxíng kěyǐ zēngjìn péngyou zhījiān de gǎnqíng.
column7: Traveling together can deepen the bond between friends.
column9: It goes with things that grow between people or in the body: 增進友誼, 增進了解, 增進健康. For plain amounts and numbers, such as 人數 or 收入, use 增加 instead.

column3: It describes businesses, families and trades that are doing well: 生意兴旺, 人丁兴旺, 香火兴旺. It is not used for a single person's success.
column4: 他的生意越来越兴旺。
column5: 他的生意越來越興旺。
column6: Tā de shēngyi yuè lái yuè xīngwàng.
column7: His business is getting more and more prosperous.
column9: It describes businesses, families and trades that are doing well: 生意興旺, 人丁興旺, 香火興旺. It is not used for a single person's success.

column3: It goes with big things: a country, a nation, a culture or an era. It often appears in the blessing 繁荣昌盛, and is less natural for a single shop, where 兴旺 fits.
column4: 祝愿祖国繁荣昌盛。
column5: 祝願祖國繁榮昌盛。
column6: Zhùyuàn zǔguó fánróng chāngshèng.
column7: May the motherland be prosperous and thriving.
column9: It goes with big things: a country, a nation, a culture or an era. It often appears in the blessing 繁榮昌盛, and is less natural for a single shop, where 興旺 fits.

column3: It goes with a custom, style, trend or belief that has become widespread: 这种风气盛行, 盛行一时. For an illness spreading, 流行 is the usual word.
column4: 这种风气在当地很盛行。
column5: 這種風氣在當地很盛行。
column6: Zhè zhǒng fēngqì zài dāngdì hěn shèngxíng.
column7: This custom is very popular in the area.
column9: It goes with a custom, style, trend or belief that has become widespread: 這種風氣盛行, 盛行一時. For an illness spreading, 流行 is the usual word.

column3: It goes with 有, 发挥 and 挖掘: 有潜力, 发挥潜力, 挖掘潜力. It can describe a person, a market, a product or a young athlete, and is always a good thing.
column4: 这个年轻人很有潜力。
column5: 這個年輕人很有潛力。
column6: Zhège niánqīngrén hěn yǒu qiánlì.
column7: This young person has a lot of potential.
column9: It goes with 有, 發揮 and 挖掘: 有潛力, 發揮潛力, 挖掘潛力. It can describe a person, a market, a product or a young athlete, and is always a good thing.

column3: It is a serious flaw in a product, design, system or person: 设计缺陷, 性格缺陷, 先天缺陷 (a birth defect). For an everyday shortcoming of a person, 缺点 is the common word.
column4: 这个产品有一个严重的缺陷。
column5: 這個產品有一個嚴重的缺陷。
column6: Zhège chǎnpǐn yǒu yī gè yánzhòng de quēxiàn.
column7: This product has a serious flaw.
column9: It is a serious flaw in a product, design, system or person: 設計缺陷, 性格缺陷, 先天缺陷 (a birth defect). For an everyday shortcoming of a person, 缺點 is the common word.

column3: 险 mostly lives in compounds: 危险, 保险 (also insurance), 冒险. On its own it describes a steep, dangerous place: 山路很险.
column4: 这条山路很险。
column5: 這條山路很險。
column6: Zhè tiáo shānlù hěn xiǎn.
column7: This mountain road is dangerous.
column9: 險 mostly lives in compounds: 危險, 保險 (also insurance), 冒險. On its own it describes a steep, dangerous place: 山路很險.

column3: It is for a state you sink into and can't easily get out of, usually a bad one: 陷入困境, 陷入危机, 陷入沉思. Falling deeply in love is also 陷入爱河.
column4: 公司陷入了困境。
column5: 公司陷入了困境。
column6: Gōngsī xiànrù le kùnjìng.
column7: The company fell into difficulty.
column9: It is for a state you sink into and can't easily get out of, usually a bad one: 陷入困境, 陷入危機, 陷入沉思. Falling deeply in love is also 陷入愛河.

column3: The serious word for poverty, common in news about 贫困地区, 贫困家庭 and 脱贫. In everyday talk, 穷 is the plain word for being poor. One suggested way to remember 贫: the phonetic part means to divide, so it is to divide one's money.
column4: 这个地区的贫困人口正在减少。
column5: 這個地區的貧困人口正在減少。
column6: Zhège dìqū de pínkùn rénkǒu zhèngzài jiǎnshǎo.
column7: The number of people living in poverty in this region is falling.
column9: The serious word for poverty, common in news about 貧困地區, 貧困家庭 and 脫貧. In everyday talk, 窮 is the plain word for being poor. One suggested way to remember 貧: the phonetic part means to divide, so it is to divide one's money.

column3: Before an unpleasant thing that happens to you, it works like 被: 挨骂, 挨饿, 挨批评, 挨打. Its other sense, to drag on or stall, shows up in 挨时间.
column4: 他因为迟到挨了老师的批评。
column5: 他因為遲到挨了老師的批評。
column6: Tā yīnwèi chídào ái le lǎoshī de pīpíng.
column7: He was scolded by the teacher for being late.
column9: Before an unpleasant thing that happens to you, it works like 被: 挨罵, 挨餓, 挨批評, 挨打. Its other sense, to drag on or stall, shows up in 挨時間.

column3: The one who is hit is the subject: 他挨打了. To do the hitting, say 打 or 打人. Like 挨骂 and 挨饿, it is a pattern that 挨 gives for things suffered.
column4: 他小时候经常挨打。
column5: 他小時候經常挨打。
column6: Tā xiǎo shíhou jīngcháng áidǎ.
column7: He was often beaten as a child.
column9: The one who is hit is the subject: 他挨打了. To do the hitting, say 打 or 打人. Like 挨罵 and 挨餓, it is a pattern that 挨 gives for things suffered.

column3: It is used for countries, parties, groups and families breaking into camps (分裂成两派), and for cell division in biology (细胞分裂). 分 is 八, to separate, over 刀, a knife: to separate with a knife.
column4: 公司内部分裂成了两派。
column5: 公司內部分裂成了兩派。
column6: Gōngsī nèibù fēnliè chéng le liǎng pài.
column7: The company split into two camps internally.
column9: It is used for countries, parties, groups and families breaking into camps (分裂成兩派), and for cell division in biology (細胞分裂). 分 is 八, to separate, over 刀, a knife: to separate with a knife.

column3: Its object is a problem or tension: 化解矛盾, 化解危机, 化解误会, 化解尴尬. The trouble is not fought but dissolved so that it no longer matters.
column4: 他用幽默化解了尴尬的气氛。
column5: 他用幽默化解了尷尬的氣氛。
column6: Tā yòng yōumò huàjiě le gāngà de qìfēn.
column7: He used humor to ease the awkward mood.
column9: Its object is a problem or tension: 化解矛盾, 化解危機, 化解誤會, 化解尷尬. The trouble is not fought but dissolved so that it no longer matters.

column3: It is done to an organization, a market or a practice that has become disorderly: 整顿市场, 整顿纪律. For tidying your own room or papers, 整理 or 收拾 is the word.
column4: 政府决定整顿市场秩序。
column5: 政府決定整頓市場秩序。
column6: Zhèngfǔ juédìng zhěngdùn shìchǎng zhìxù.
column7: The government decided to clean up the market order.
column9: It is done to an organization, a market or a practice that has become disorderly: 整頓市場, 整頓紀律. For tidying your own room or papers, 整理 or 收拾 is the word.

column3: It means to deal firmly with a mess, with objects such as 环境, 河道 and 交通: 整治环境. Spoken, 整治 someone is also to give them a hard time.
column4: 这个城市正在整治环境。
column5: 這個城市正在整治環境。
column6: Zhège chéngshì zhèngzài zhěngzhì huánjìng.
column7: This city is cleaning up its environment.
column9: It means to deal firmly with a mess, with objects such as 環境, 河道 and 交通: 整治環境. Spoken, 整治 someone is also to give them a hard time.

column3: Mostly in front of a noun: 应急措施, 应急预案, 应急灯, 应急电话, all things made ready for an emergency.
column4: 我们准备了一些应急用品。
column5: 我們準備了一些應急用品。
column6: Wǒmen zhǔnbèi le yīxiē yìngjí yòngpǐn.
column7: We prepared some emergency supplies.
column9: Mostly in front of a noun: 應急措施, 應急預案, 應急燈, 應急電話, all things made ready for an emergency.

column3: Its object is a difficulty or change that has to be met: 应对挑战, 应对危机, 应对变化. It sounds a little more formal than 对付.
column4: 我们要学会应对压力。
column5: 我們要學會應對壓力。
column6: Wǒmen yào xuéhuì yìngduì yālì.
column7: We need to learn to cope with stress.
column9: Its object is a difficulty or change that has to be met: 應對挑戰, 應對危機, 應對變化. It sounds a little more formal than 對付.

column3: The object is a risk or harm that has not happened yet: 防范风险, 防范诈骗, 防范措施. It stresses staying on guard in advance.
column4: 大家要提高防范意识，小心诈骗。
column5: 大家要提高防範意識，小心詐騙。
column6: Dàjiā yào tígāo fángfàn yìshí, xiǎoxīn zhàpiàn.
column7: Everyone should be on guard and watch out for scams.
column9: The object is a risk or harm that has not happened yet: 防範風險, 防範詐騙, 防範措施. It stresses staying on guard in advance.

column3: 掉 after a verb shows something is gone or removed: 去掉, 删掉, 扔掉, 忘掉. 去掉 is the general word for taking away part of something.
column4: 请把这个词去掉。
column5: 請把這個詞去掉。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège cí qùdiào.
column7: Please remove this word.
column9: 掉 after a verb shows something is gone or removed: 去掉, 刪掉, 扔掉, 忘掉. 去掉 is the general word for taking away part of something.

column3: Mostly for changing a car, a room or a machine so that it looks or works differently: 改装汽车, 改装房间. Less often it means changing costume or repackaging.
column4: 他想把阁楼改装成书房。
column5: 他想把閣樓改裝成書房。
column6: Tā xiǎng bǎ gélóu gǎizhuāng chéng shūfáng.
column7: He wants to convert the attic into a study.
column9: Mostly for changing a car, a room or a machine so that it looks or works differently: 改裝汽車, 改裝房間. Less often it means changing costume or repackaging.

column3: A written word for if, found on notices and in formal writing, where speech says 如果: 若有问题, 若是, 假若. It also means like in set phrases such as 欣喜若狂 and 旁若无人.
column4: 若有问题，请随时告诉我。
column5: 若有問題，請隨時告訴我。
column6: Ruò yǒu wèntí, qǐng suíshí gàosu wǒ.
column7: If you have any questions, please tell me anytime.
column9: A written word for if, found on notices and in formal writing, where speech says 如果: 若有問題, 若是, 假若. It also means like in set phrases such as 欣喜若狂 and 旁若無人.
