column3: A short, written form of 虽然: it opens the "although" clause, and the second clause usually answers with 但是, 可是 or 却.
column4: 他虽累，却很高兴。
column5: 他雖累，卻很高興。
column6: Tā suī lèi, què hěn gāoxìng.
column7: Tired as he is, he is very happy.
column9: A short, written form of 雖然: it opens the "although" clause, and the second clause usually answers with 但是, 可是 or 卻.

column3: Used in pairs, 要么…要么…, to set out two choices; on its own at the start of a sentence it offers an alternative, like "or else".
column4: 要么你去，要么我去。
column5: 要麼你去，要麼我去。
column6: Yàome nǐ qù, yàome wǒ qù.
column7: Either you go or I go.
column9: Used in pairs, 要麼…要麼…, to set out two choices; on its own at the start of a sentence it offers an alternative, like "or else".

column3: It opens a clause that names a whole group, and the main clause usually answers with 都 or 就: 凡是…都….
column4: 凡是来过的人都喜欢这里。
column5: 凡是來過的人都喜歡這裡。
column6: Fánshì lái guo de rén dōu xǐhuan zhèlǐ.
column7: Everyone who has been here likes it.
column9: It opens a clause that names a whole group, and the main clause usually answers with 都 or 就: 凡是…都….

column3: A more written way to say 就是: it points to something as exactly so. It can also mean "even if", with 也 or 都 in the next clause.
column4: 这便是我的家。
column5: 這便是我的家。
column6: Zhè biànshì wǒ de jiā.
column7: This is my home.
column9: A more written way to say 就是: it points to something as exactly so. It can also mean "even if", with 也 or 都 in the next clause.

column3: It marks a turn against what came before: the clause that follows says what is actually the case. 却 alone is the usual everyday "but".
column4: 看上去容易，做起来却是另一回事。
column5: 看上去容易，做起來卻是另一回事。
column6: Kàn shàngqu róngyì, zuò qǐlai quèshì lìng yī huí shì.
column7: It looks easy, but doing it is another matter.
column9: It marks a turn against what came before: the clause that follows says what is actually the case. 卻 alone is the usual everyday "but".

column3: Means "like" or "as if", often in the frame 好似…一般. It is more written than the everyday 好像.
column4: 她笑起来好似春天的花。
column5: 她笑起來好似春天的花。
column6: Tā xiào qǐlai hǎosì chūntiān de huā.
column7: When she smiles she is like a spring flower.
column9: Means "like" or "as if", often in the frame 好似…一般. It is more written than the everyday 好像.

column3: Weighs options and trade-offs: 衡量利弊. It also judges something against a yardstick: 用…来衡量, 衡量一个人的标准.
column4: 做决定之前要仔细衡量利弊。
column5: 做決定之前要仔細衡量利弊。
column6: Zuò juédìng zhīqián yào zǐxì héngliáng lìbì.
column7: Before making a decision, weigh the pros and cons carefully.
column9: Weighs options and trade-offs: 衡量利弊. It also judges something against a yardstick: 用…來衡量, 衡量一個人的標準.

column3: Seen mostly inside compounds such as 评价, 评论 and 好评. On its own it is a verb: 评一评谁对 means to judge who is right, 被评为优秀教师 to be named an outstanding teacher.
column4: 他被评为优秀员工。
column5: 他被評為優秀員工。
column6: Tā bèi píng wéi yōuxiù yuángōng.
column7: He was named an outstanding employee.
column9: Seen mostly inside compounds such as 評價, 評論 and 好評. On its own it is a verb: 評一評誰對 means to judge who is right, 被評為優秀教師 to be named an outstanding teacher.

column3: Takes an object you check: 查看邮件, 查看记录, 查看资料. It is a more deliberate look than plain 看.
column4: 请查看你的邮件。
column5: 請查看你的郵件。
column6: Qǐng chákàn nǐ de yóujiàn.
column7: Please check your mail.
column9: Takes an object you check: 查看郵件, 查看記錄, 查看資料. It is a more deliberate look than plain 看.

column3: Done by an expert, on things like antiques, art, handwriting or DNA: 鉴定真伪, 鉴定结果. On its own, 鉴 was an ancient bronze mirror, and it also means to examine or scrutinize.
column4: 专家正在鉴定这幅画的真假。
column5: 專家正在鑑定這幅畫的真假。
column6: Zhuānjiā zhèngzài jiàndìng zhè fú huà de zhēnjiǎ.
column7: Experts are authenticating this painting.
column9: Done by an expert, on things like antiques, art, handwriting or DNA: 鑑定真偽, 鑑定結果. On its own, 鑑 was an ancient bronze mirror, and it also means to examine or scrutinize.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: 监督政府, 监督工作, and 接受监督 for being under oversight.
column4: 市民有权监督政府的工作。
column5: 市民有權監督政府的工作。
column6: Shìmín yǒu quán jiāndū zhèngfǔ de gōngzuò.
column7: Citizens have the right to oversee the government's work.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: 監督政府, 監督工作, and 接受監督 for being under oversight.

column3: A policy-news word: a new measure is tried first in one place, then rolled out. It is both a noun and a verb. Taiwan more often says 试办.
column4: 这项新政策先在三个城市试点。
column5: 這項新政策先在三個城市試點。
column6: Zhè xiàng xīn zhèngcè xiān zài sān gè chéngshì shìdiǎn.
column7: The new policy is being piloted in three cities first.
column9: A policy-news word: a new measure is tried first in one place, then rolled out. It is both a noun and a verb. Taiwan more often says 試辦.

column3: Formal; sits before a verb for real, concrete action: 切实解决, 切实保障. 切实可行 means "practical and workable".
column4: 我们必须切实解决这个问题。
column5: 我們必須切實解決這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen bìxū qièshí jiějué zhège wèntí.
column7: We must really solve this problem.
column9: Formal; sits before a verb for real, concrete action: 切實解決, 切實保障. 切實可行 means "practical and workable".

column3: Praises both things and people's skills or work: 基础扎实 is a solid foundation, 功底扎实 sound skills, 工作扎实 thorough work.
column4: 他的中文基础很扎实。
column5: 他的中文基礎很紮實。
column6: Tā de Zhōngwén jīchǔ hěn zhāshi.
column7: His Chinese foundation is very solid.
column9: Praises both things and people's skills or work: 基礎紮實 is a solid foundation, 功底紮實 sound skills, 工作紮實 thorough work.

column3: Suits the unknown or the new: 探索宇宙, 探索新方法. It works as a noun too, "exploration".
column4: 科学家一直在探索未知的世界。
column5: 科學家一直在探索未知的世界。
column6: Kēxuéjiā yīzhí zài tànsuǒ wèizhī de shìjiè.
column7: Scientists have always explored the unknown world.
column9: Suits the unknown or the new: 探索宇宙, 探索新方法. It works as a noun too, "exploration".

column3: Short for 科学研究. It is mostly a noun or a modifier: 科研人员, 科研经费, 科研成果.
column4: 她在大学从事科研工作。
column5: 她在大學從事科研工作。
column6: Tā zài dàxué cóngshì kēyán gōngzuò.
column7: She does scientific research at a university.
column9: Short for 科學研究. It is mostly a noun or a modifier: 科研人員, 科研經費, 科研成果.

column3: Short for 调查研究: going out to investigate and then analyzing. Common in business and government: 市场调研, 调研报告. Taiwan more often says 调查.
column4: 公司派他去做市场调研。
column5: 公司派他去做市場調研。
column6: Gōngsī pài tā qù zuò shìchǎng diàoyán.
column7: The company sent him to do market research.
column9: Short for 調查研究: going out to investigate and then analyzing. Common in business and government: 市場調研, 調研報告. Taiwan more often says 調查.

column3: Noun and adjective: 有创意 is "creative" and 创意十足 "full of creativity". It also names a field, as in 创意产业.
column4: 这个广告很有创意。
column5: 這個廣告很有創意。
column6: Zhège guǎnggào hěn yǒu chuàngyì.
column7: This ad is very creative.
column9: Noun and adjective: 有創意 is "creative" and 創意十足 "full of creativity". It also names a field, as in 創意產業.

column3: Short for 研究开发, "research and development", with 发 as in 开发. Common in 研发中心 and 研发出, as in 研发出新产品 ("come up with a new product").
column4: 这家公司专门研发新药。
column5: 這家公司專門研發新藥。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānmén yánfā xīn yào.
column7: This company specializes in developing new drugs.
column9: Short for 研究開發, "research and development", with 發 as in 開發. Common in 研發中心 and 研發出, as in 研發出新產品 ("come up with a new product").

column3: 科技 is short for 科学技术, and 高科技 modifies a noun: 高科技产品, 高科技产业. 高 makes a pattern of "high" words: 高水平, 高收入, 高质量.
column4: 这座城市有很多高科技公司。
column5: 這座城市有很多高科技公司。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō gāokējì gōngsī.
column7: This city has many high-tech companies.
column9: 科技 is short for 科學技術, and 高科技 modifies a noun: 高科技產品, 高科技產業. 高 makes a pattern of "high" words: 高水平, 高收入, 高質量.

column3: Used in the pattern 把 A 当成 B, "take A for B": it can be a fair view or a mistake, as in 把盐当成糖. Here 当 is read dàng; as dāng it means to be, to act as, or when.
column4: 别把我当成外人。
column5: 別把我當成外人。
column6: Bié bǎ wǒ dàngchéng wàirén.
column7: Don't treat me like an outsider.
column9: Used in the pattern 把 A 當成 B, "take A for B": it can be a fair view or a mistake, as in 把鹽當成糖. Here 當 is read dàng; as dāng it means to be, to act as, or when.

column3: Pattern 把 A 看作 B, "regard A as B". It states a view or judgment, while 当成 can also mean mistaking one thing for another.
column4: 人们把他看作英雄。
column5: 人們把他看作英雄。
column6: Rénmen bǎ tā kànzuò yīngxióng.
column7: People regard him as a hero.
column9: Pattern 把 A 看作 B, "regard A as B". It states a view or judgment, while 當成 can also mean mistaking one thing for another.

column3: A forecasting word: 看好这家公司 means expecting it to do well, and 不被看好 means nobody expects it to. Read kān hǎo, it means to keep an eye on something.
column4: 大家都看好这家公司的前景。
column5: 大家都看好這家公司的前景。
column6: Dàjiā dōu kànhǎo zhè jiā gōngsī de qiánjǐng.
column7: Everyone is optimistic about this company's prospects.
column9: A forecasting word: 看好這家公司 means expecting it to do well, and 不被看好 means nobody expects it to. Read kān hǎo, it means to keep an eye on something.

column3: Formal. What gets 采纳 is a suggestion, opinion, proposal or advice (采纳建议, 意见被采纳); for accepting a gift or an invitation, say 接受.
column4: 经理采纳了我的建议。
column5: 經理採納了我的建議。
column6: Jīnglǐ cǎinà le wǒ de jiànyì.
column7: The manager took up my suggestion.
column9: Formal. What gets 採納 is a suggestion, opinion, proposal or advice (採納建議, 意見被採納); for accepting a gift or an invitation, say 接受.

column3: A written, fairly formal word whose object is experience or methods (借鉴经验, 借鉴别人的做法); the subject takes a lesson from someone else's example, not borrowing a thing. 鉴 is a bronze mirror used in ancient times, and also something that serves as a warning or a lesson.
column4: 我们可以借鉴其他国家的经验。
column5: 我們可以借鑒其他國家的經驗。
column6: Wǒmen kěyǐ jièjiàn qítā guójiā de jīngyàn.
column7: We can learn from other countries' experience.
column9: A written, fairly formal word whose object is experience or methods (借鑒經驗, 借鑒別人的做法); the subject takes a lesson from someone else's example, not borrowing a thing. 鑒 is a bronze mirror used in ancient times, and also something that serves as a warning or a lesson.

column3: Set against emotion: 保持理智 is to stay level-headed, 失去理智 to lose control. It also works as an adjective: 很理智 and 不理智 are both normal.
column4: 遇到问题时，要保持理智。
column5: 遇到問題時，要保持理智。
column6: Yùdào wèntí shí, yào bǎochí lǐzhì.
column7: When you run into a problem, stay calm and rational.
column9: Set against emotion: 保持理智 is to stay level-headed, 失去理智 to lose control. It also works as an adjective: 很理智 and 不理智 are both normal.

column3: The 素 family: 元素 is an element, 因素 is any factor, and 要素 is an essential one, as in 基本要素 or 成功的要素.
column4: 教育有三个基本要素。
column5: 教育有三個基本要素。
column6: Jiàoyù yǒu sān gè jīběn yàosù.
column7: Education has three basic elements.
column9: The 素 family: 元素 is an element, 因素 is any factor, and 要素 is an essential one, as in 基本要素 or 成功的要素.

column3: Put after a name for a chemical element (氧元素, 氢元素), and also used loosely for a feature or ingredient of something, as in 时尚元素 and 文化元素.
column4: 水由氢元素和氧元素组成。
column5: 水由氫元素和氧元素組成。
column6: Shuǐ yóu qīng yuánsù hé yǎng yuánsù zǔchéng.
column7: Water is made of the elements hydrogen and oxygen.
column9: Put after a name for a chemical element (氧元素, 氫元素), and also used loosely for a feature or ingredient of something, as in 時尚元素 and 文化元素.

column3: A person's overall quality: education, manners and ability together. Common in 提高素质, 高素质, 国民素质 and 素质教育, and often said of staff and citizens.
column4: 这个公司很重视员工的素质。
column5: 這個公司很重視員工的素質。
column6: Zhège gōngsī hěn zhòngshì yuángōng de sùzhì.
column7: This company cares a lot about the quality of its staff.
column9: A person's overall quality: education, manners and ability together. Common in 提高素質, 高素質, 國民素質 and 素質教育, and often said of staff and citizens.

column3: An abstract level or aspect of an issue, not a physical floor. It usually comes in 在……层面上 or 从……层面, as in 法律层面 and 各个层面.
column4: 我们要从不同层面分析这个问题。
column5: 我們要從不同層面分析這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen yào cóng bùtóng céngmiàn fēnxī zhège wèntí.
column7: We need to analyze this problem from different levels.
column9: An abstract level or aspect of an issue, not a physical floor. It usually comes in 在……層面上 or 從……層面, as in 法律層面 and 各個層面.

column3: A verb for telling things apart or sorting them into kinds: 区分A和B, 难以区分, 区分为三类. The noun for the difference itself is 区别.
column4: 这两个词的意思很接近，很难区分。
column5: 這兩個詞的意思很接近，很難區分。
column6: Zhè liǎng gè cí de yìsi hěn jiējìn, hěn nán qūfēn.
column7: These two words are close in meaning and hard to tell apart.
column9: A verb for telling things apart or sorting them into kinds: 區分A和B, 難以區分, 區分為三類. The noun for the difference itself is 區別.

column3: Mostly the front of a word, meaning 'original' or 'former': 原来, 原价, 原文, 原因. The flat-land sense shows in 平原 and 草原. 元 and 原 were once used interchangeably for "origin".
column4: 他原是老师。
column5: 他原是老師。
column6: Tā yuán shì lǎoshī.
column7: He was originally a teacher.
column9: Mostly the front of a word, meaning 'original' or 'former': 原來, 原價, 原文, 原因. The flat-land sense shows in 平原 and 草原. 元 and 原 were once used interchangeably for "origin".

column3: As a word it is written Chinese meaning 'in, at, to, than', and it hides inside everyday compounds: 关于, 由于, 终于, 位于, 属于. It is also a common surname.
column4: 他毕业于北京大学。
column5: 他畢業於北京大學。
column6: Tā bìyè yú Běijīng Dàxué.
column7: He graduated from Peking University.
column9: As a word it is written Chinese meaning 'in, at, to, than', and it hides inside everyday compounds: 關於, 由於, 終於, 位於, 屬於. It is also a common surname.

column3: Rarely stands alone in speech: 因为, 因此 and 原因 carry it. Alone it is formal and written, as in 因病请假 (off sick) and 因故取消 (canceled for some reason).
column4: 他因病没来上课。
column5: 他因病沒來上課。
column6: Tā yīn bìng méi lái shàngkè.
column7: He missed class because he was ill.
column9: Rarely stands alone in speech: 因為, 因此 and 原因 carry it. Alone it is formal and written, as in 因病請假 (off sick) and 因故取消 (canceled for some reason).

column3: A formal connector that points back at what was just said: 'for this reason' or 'to that end'. It opens the next clause, as in 为此我们决定….
column4: 比赛快到了，为此我们每天练习。
column5: 比賽快到了，為此我們每天練習。
column6: Bǐsài kuài dào le, wèicǐ wǒmen měitiān liànxí.
column7: The match is coming up, so we practice every day.
column9: A formal connector that points back at what was just said: 'for this reason' or 'to that end'. It opens the next clause, as in 為此我們決定….

column3: Formal, common in news and reports. Its object is a topic, a matter or a sum (涉及隐私, 涉及金额), and it often takes 到: 涉及到.
column4: 这件事涉及很多人。
column5: 這件事涉及很多人。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì shèjí hěn duō rén.
column7: This matter involves a lot of people.
column9: Formal, common in news and reports. Its object is a topic, a matter or a sum (涉及隱私, 涉及金額), and it often takes 到: 涉及到.

column3: Usually a noun after 有 or 没有 (有关联, 毫无关联), or a verb in A与B相关联 and A与B有关联. Close to 关系, but mostly for links between things or data rather than between people.
column4: 这两件事之间有什么关联？
column5: 這兩件事之間有什麼關聯？
column6: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì zhījiān yǒu shénme guānlián?
column7: What is the connection between these two things?
column9: Usually a noun after 有 or 沒有 (有關聯, 毫無關聯), or a verb in A與B相關聯 and A與B有關聯. Close to 關係, but mostly for links between things or data rather than between people.

column3: Goes in front of another word: 对外贸易, 对外关系, and 对外开放 for a place open to the public. The opposite is 对内.
column4: 这家博物馆下个月对外开放。
column5: 這家博物館下個月對外開放。
column6: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn xià gè yuè duìwài kāifàng.
column7: This museum opens to the public next month.
column9: Goes in front of another word: 對外貿易, 對外關係, and 對外開放 for a place open to the public. The opposite is 對內.

column3: More formal than 找工作, and it takes no object of its own. It is common in 求职信 (cover letter), 求职者 (job seeker) and 求职网站 (job site).
column4: 他毕业后开始求职。
column5: 他畢業後開始求職。
column6: Tā bìyè hòu kāishǐ qiúzhí.
column7: He started looking for a job after graduating.
column9: More formal than 找工作, and it takes no object of its own. It is common in 求職信 (cover letter), 求職者 (job seeker) and 求職網站 (job site).

column3: The post someone holds in an organization, more official than 工作: 工作岗位, 岗位职责, 岗位招聘. It also names the spot where a guard stands duty.
column4: 他在这个岗位上工作了十年。
column5: 他在這個崗位上工作了十年。
column6: Tā zài zhège gǎngwèi shàng gōngzuò le shí nián.
column7: He has worked in this position for ten years.
column9: The post someone holds in an organization, more official than 工作: 工作崗位, 崗位職責, 崗位招聘. It also names the spot where a guard stands duty.

column3: The duty that comes with a role: 老师的职责, 岗位职责, with the verbs 履行 and 尽. 责任 is wider and also covers blame, as in 负责任 and 追究责任.
column4: 保护学生的安全是老师的职责。
column5: 保護學生的安全是老師的職責。
column6: Bǎohù xuéshēng de ānquán shì lǎoshī de zhízé.
column7: Keeping students safe is a teacher's duty.
column9: The duty that comes with a role: 老師的職責, 崗位職責, with the verbs 履行 and 盡. 責任 is wider and also covers blame, as in 負責任 and 追究責任.

column3: A desk, usually with drawers, for writing. 书桌 is the plainer everyday word for a study desk and 办公桌 the office one. This 台 is a table-like fitting, as in 梳妆台 and 柜台.
column4: 他的写字台上放着很多书。
column5: 他的寫字檯上放著很多書。
column6: Tā de xiězìtái shàng fàng zhe hěn duō shū.
column7: There are many books on his desk.
column9: A desk, usually with drawers, for writing. 書桌 is the plainer everyday word for a study desk and 辦公桌 the office one. This 檯 is a table-like fitting, as in 櫃檯.

column3: Two common uses: the fixed number of official posts an organization may have (有编制 means being on its permanent staff), and putting together a plan or budget (编制预算).
column4: 他在学校有编制，工作很稳定。
column5: 他在學校有編制，工作很穩定。
column6: Tā zài xuéxiào yǒu biānzhì, gōngzuò hěn wěndìng.
column7: He has a permanent post at a school, so his job is stable.
column9: Two common uses: the fixed number of official posts an organization may have (有編制 means being on its permanent staff), and putting together a plan or budget (編制預算).

column3: A group working toward a shared goal, as in a company or project: 团队合作, 团队精神. A sports team is usually just 队, as in 篮球队.
column4: 我们的团队有五个人。
column5: 我們的團隊有五個人。
column6: Wǒmen de tuánduì yǒu wǔ gè rén.
column7: Our team has five people.
column9: A group working toward a shared goal, as in a company or project: 團隊合作, 團隊精神. A sports team is usually just 隊, as in 籃球隊.

column3: Often about drawing something toward you: 招来麻烦 (bring trouble), 招蚊子 (attract mosquitoes). For hiring or enrolling, the organization does the 招: 招生, 招聘. It also means a move or trick: 这一招, 高招 (a smart move), 绝招, and 没招了 (out of ideas).
column4: 他向我招手。
column5: 他向我招手。
column6: Tā xiàng wǒ zhāo shǒu.
column7: He waved to me.
column9: Often about drawing something toward you: 招來麻煩 (bring trouble), 招蚊子 (attract mosquitoes). For hiring or enrolling, the organization does the 招: 招生, 招聘. It also means a move or trick: 這一招, 高招 (a smart move), 絕招, and 沒招了 (out of ideas).

column3: The object is an organization or enterprise: 创办公司, 创办学校, 创办杂志. The founder is the 创办人.
column4: 他二十年前创办了这家公司。
column5: 他二十年前創辦了這家公司。
column6: Tā èrshí nián qián chuàngbàn le zhè jiā gōngsī.
column7: He founded this company twenty years ago.
column9: The object is an organization or enterprise: 創辦公司, 創辦學校, 創辦雜誌. The founder is the 創辦人.

column3: Fits things built up from nothing, often abstract or technical: 创建体系, 创建平台, and on a computer 创建账号, 创建文件夹. For a school or company, 创办 is more usual. One scholar sees 建 as originally a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.
column4: 请先创建一个新账号。
column5: 請先創建一個新帳號。
column6: Qǐng xiān chuàngjiàn yī gè xīn zhànghào.
column7: Please create a new account first.
column9: Fits things built up from nothing, often abstract or technical: 創建體系, 創建平臺, and on a computer 創建帳號, 創建文件夾. For a school or company, 創辦 is more usual. One scholar sees 建 as originally a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.

column3: Used for events, campaigns and projects: 策划活动, 策划方案. It is also the noun for the planning itself and, as a job title, for the planner.
column4: 她负责策划这次活动。
column5: 她負責策劃這次活動。
column6: Tā fùzé cèhuà zhè cì huódòng.
column7: She is in charge of planning this event.
column9: Used for events, campaigns and projects: 策劃活動, 策劃方案. It is also the noun for the planning itself and, as a job title, for the planner.

column3: A decision made at the level of leaders or policy, not an everyday choice (that is 决定): 决策者, 决策层, 科学决策. It can also be a verb, to make policy.
column4: 这是公司领导的重要决策。
column5: 這是公司領導的重要決策。
column6: Zhè shì gōngsī lǐngdǎo de zhòngyào juécè.
column7: This is an important decision by the company's leaders.
column9: A decision made at the level of leaders or policy, not an everyday choice (that is 決定): 決策者, 決策層, 科學決策. It can also be a verb, to make policy.

column3: Opens up something new, often on a grand scale: 开创新局面, 开创新时代, 开创先河. Its objects are eras, paths and causes, where 创办 takes a company or school.
column4: 这项发明开创了一个新时代。
column5: 這項發明開創了一個新時代。
column6: Zhè xiàng fāmíng kāichuàng le yī gè xīn shídài.
column7: This invention opened a new era.
column9: Opens up something new, often on a grand scale: 開創新局面, 開創新時代, 開創先河. Its objects are eras, paths and causes, where 創辦 takes a company or school.

column3: Switches on a road, line or service so people can use it: 开通地铁, 开通账号, 开通会员. With a neutral-tone second syllable, kāitong, the word means open-minded.
column4: 你可以在手机上开通这项服务。
column5: 你可以在手機上開通這項服務。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zài shǒujī shàng kāitōng zhè xiàng fúwù.
column7: You can activate this service on your phone.
column9: Switches on a road, line or service so people can use it: 開通地鐵, 開通帳號, 開通會員. With a neutral-tone second syllable, kāitong, the word means open-minded.

column3: The head office of a company or organization, as opposed to its branches (分公司, 分部). 总 marks the top, main one, as in 总经理 and 总统.
column4: 公司总部在上海。
column5: 公司總部在上海。
column6: Gōngsī zǒngbù zài Shànghǎi.
column7: The company's headquarters is in Shanghai.
column9: The head office of a company or organization, as opposed to its branches (分公司, 分部). 總 marks the top, main one, as in 總經理 and 總統.

column3: A senior title, usually with the field in front: 技术总监, 创意总监, 财务总监, the head of that function in a company.
column4: 他是我们公司的技术总监。
column5: 他是我們公司的技術總監。
column6: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de jìshù zǒngjiān.
column7: He is our company's technical director.
column9: A senior title, usually with the field in front: 技術總監, 創意總監, 財務總監, the head of that function in a company.

column3: The top manager of a company; deputies are 副总经理. People often address a boss by surname plus 总, so Mr. Wang is 王总.
column4: 总经理正在会议室开会。
column5: 總經理正在會議室開會。
column6: Zǒngjīnglǐ zhèngzài huìyìshì kāihuì.
column7: The general manager is in a meeting in the conference room.
column9: The top manager of a company; deputies are 副總經理. People often address a boss by surname plus 總, so Mr. Wang is 王總.

column3: Mostly found in set phrases and names: 工商业, 工商界, 工商管理 (business administration), and banks and offices named 工商.
column4: 他在大学学的是工商管理。
column5: 他在大學學的是工商管理。
column6: Tā zài dàxué xué de shì gōngshāng guǎnlǐ.
column7: He studied business administration at college.
column9: Mostly found in set phrases and names: 工商業, 工商界, 工商管理 (business administration), and banks and offices named 工商.

column3: Joining a group that already exists: a franchise (加盟店, 加盟费), a team, a label or a cast. A franchisee is a 加盟商.
column4: 他决定加盟一家连锁咖啡店。
column5: 他決定加盟一家連鎖咖啡店。
column6: Tā juédìng jiāméng yī jiā liánsuǒ kāfēidiàn.
column7: He decided to join a chain coffee shop as a franchisee.
column9: Joining a group that already exists: a franchise (加盟店, 加盟費), a team, a label or a cast. A franchisee is a 加盟商.

column3: Used for companies and assets (企业重组, 资产重组) and in science for 基因重组, recombining genes. 重 is read chóng here, meaning again; for heavy, it is read zhòng.
column4: 公司决定重组管理团队。
column5: 公司決定重組管理團隊。
column6: Gōngsī juédìng chóngzǔ guǎnlǐ tuánduì.
column7: The company decided to reorganize its management team.
column9: Used for companies and assets (企業重組, 資產重組) and in science for 基因重組, recombining genes. 重 is read chóng here, meaning again; for heavy, it is read zhòng.

column3: The things rebuilt are usually ones that were destroyed or lost: 重建家园, 重建信心, 重建秩序. 重 means again here, as in 重新 and 重做. One scholar sees 建 as originally a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.
column4: 地震后，他们开始重建家园。
column5: 地震後，他們開始重建家園。
column6: Dìzhèn hòu, tāmen kāishǐ chóngjiàn jiāyuán.
column7: After the earthquake, they began to rebuild their homes.
column9: The things rebuilt are usually ones that were destroyed or lost: 重建家園, 重建信心, 重建秩序. 重 means again here, as in 重新 and 重做. One scholar sees 建 as originally a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.

column3: How an organization or system runs: 公司运作, 正常运作, 运作机制. It can also be a verb, to run or manage something. For a machine turning, 运转 is the word.
column4: 这家公司的运作很规范。
column5: 這家公司的運作很規範。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de yùnzuò hěn guīfàn.
column7: This company's operations are very well regulated.
column9: How an organization or system runs: 公司運作, 正常運作, 運作機制. It can also be a verb, to run or manage something. For a machine turning, 運轉 is the word.

column3: Builds something abstract or technical, such as a system, framework, model or platform: 构建体系, 构建模型. For a building, 建造 is more usual.
column4: 我们正在构建一个新的系统。
column5: 我們正在構建一個新的系統。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài gòujiàn yī gè xīn de xìtǒng.
column7: We are building a new system.
column9: Builds something abstract or technical, such as a system, framework, model or platform: 構建體系, 構建模型. For a building, 建造 is more usual.

column3: It began as forging metal, as in 打造一把剑. Today it often means building something up with care: 打造品牌, 打造团队, 打造精品.
column4: 公司想打造一个新的品牌。
column5: 公司想打造一個新的品牌。
column6: Gōngsī xiǎng dǎzào yī gè xīn de pǐnpái.
column7: The company wants to build up a new brand.
column9: It began as forging metal, as in 打造一把劍. Today it often means building something up with care: 打造品牌, 打造團隊, 打造精品.

column3: A forum or discussion meeting where invited people give their views: 召开座谈会, 举行座谈会, 专家座谈会, 家长座谈会. 座谈 is the verb.
column4: 学校明天下午举行家长座谈会。
column5: 學校明天下午舉行家長座談會。
column6: Xuéxiào míngtiān xiàwǔ jǔxíng jiāzhǎng zuòtánhuì.
column7: The school is holding a parents' forum tomorrow afternoon.
column9: A forum or discussion meeting where invited people give their views: 召開座談會, 舉行座談會, 專家座談會, 家長座談會. 座談 is the verb.

column3: A topic for formal discussion: an item on a meeting's agenda or an issue in public debate, as in 会议议题, 讨论议题, 热门议题. Casual chat topics are 话题.
column4: 今天会议的主要议题是明年的预算。
column5: 今天會議的主要議題是明年的預算。
column6: Jīntiān huìyì de zhǔyào yìtí shì míngnián de yùsuàn.
column7: The main topic of today's meeting is next year's budget.
column9: A topic for formal discussion: an item on a meeting's agenda or an issue in public debate, as in 會議議題, 討論議題, 熱門議題. Casual chat topics are 話題.

column3: A top-level meeting, usually of national leaders (领导人峰会, G20峰会), and also of leading figures in a field (科技峰会). The usual verb is 举行.
column4: 两国领导人将在下周举行峰会。
column5: 兩國領導人將在下週舉行峰會。
column6: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén jiāng zài xià zhōu jǔxíng fēnghuì.
column7: The two countries' leaders will hold a summit next week.
column9: A top-level meeting, usually of national leaders (領導人峰會, G20峰會), and also of leading figures in a field (科技峰會). The usual verb is 舉行.

column3: A formal meeting with a visitor, official or journalists: 会见记者, 会见外宾, 会见客人. It is the news-report word; friends meeting up say 见面.
column4: 总统会见了来访的外国代表团。
column5: 總統會見了來訪的外國代表團。
column6: Zǒngtǒng huìjiàn le láifǎng de wàiguó dàibiǎotuán.
column7: The president met with the visiting foreign delegation.
column9: A formal meeting with a visitor, official or journalists: 會見記者, 會見外賓, 會見客人. It is the news-report word; friends meeting up say 見面.

column3: Parties talk things over to reach an agreement: 协商解决, 通过协商, 协商一致. It is more formal than 商量.
column4: 双方通过协商解决了问题。
column5: 雙方通過協商解決了問題。
column6: Shuāngfāng tōngguò xiéshāng jiějué le wèntí.
column7: The two sides solved the problem through consultation.
column9: Parties talk things over to reach an agreement: 協商解決, 通過協商, 協商一致. It is more formal than 商量.

column3: As a verb it means to coordinate people or departments (协调各部门); as an adjective, things that fit together well, such as colors. 调 is read tiáo here, to harmonize; read diào, it covers senses like to investigate.
column4: 经理负责协调各部门的工作。
column5: 經理負責協調各部門的工作。
column6: Jīnglǐ fùzé xiétiáo gè bùmén de gōngzuò.
column7: The manager is responsible for coordinating the departments' work.
column9: As a verb it means to coordinate people or departments (協調各部門); as an adjective, things that fit together well, such as colors. 調 is read tiáo here, to harmonize; read diào, it covers senses like to investigate.

column3: A membership organization for a trade, sport or hobby: 足球协会, 律师协会, 摄影协会. Its members are 会员.
column4: 她加入了本地的摄影协会。
column5: 她加入了本地的攝影協會。
column6: Tā jiārù le běndì de shèyǐng xiéhuì.
column7: She joined the local photography association.
column9: A membership organization for a trade, sport or hobby: 足球協會, 律師協會, 攝影協會. Its members are 會員.

column3: A formal, written verb: you 听取 opinions, reports or suggestions, as in 听取意见 and 听取汇报. For everyday listening, say 听.
column4: 我们会认真听取大家的意见。
column5: 我們會認真聽取大家的意見。
column6: Wǒmen huì rènzhēn tīngqǔ dàjiā de yìjiàn.
column7: We will listen carefully to everyone's opinions.
column9: A formal, written verb: you 聽取 opinions, reports or suggestions, as in 聽取意見 and 聽取匯報. For everyday listening, say 聽.

column3: The head of a society, club or association, the 会 of 学生会 and 商会. The 长 here is the same one as in 处长, 司长 and 校长: the person in charge. Read zhǎng, 长 means chief; read cháng, it means long.
column4: 他当了学生会的会长。
column5: 他當了學生會的會長。
column6: Tā dāng le xuéshēnghuì de huìzhǎng.
column7: He became the president of the student association.
column9: The head of a society, club or association, the 會 of 學生會 and 商會. The 長 here is the same one as in 處長, 司長 and 校長: the person in charge. Read zhǎng, 長 means chief; read cháng, it means long.

column3: The head of a 处, a division of a government office or large organization. In a mainland ministry it ranks below a 司长 and above a 科长.
column4: 我们处长今天出差了。
column5: 我們處長今天出差了。
column6: Wǒmen chùzhǎng jīntiān chūchāi le.
column7: Our division chief is away on a business trip today.
column9: The head of a 處, a division of a government office or large organization. In a mainland ministry it ranks below a 司長 and above a 科長.

column3: The head of a 司, a department directly under a ministry. In a mainland ministry a 司长 ranks below the 部长 (minister) and above a 处长.
column4: 教育部司长出席了会议。
column5: 教育部司長出席了會議。
column6: Jiàoyù bù sīzhǎng chūxí le huìyì.
column7: The department director of the Ministry of Education attended the meeting.
column9: The head of a 司, a department directly under a ministry. In a mainland ministry a 司長 ranks below the 部長 (minister) and above a 處長.

column3: A verb and a noun: you 约定 a time or place with someone, and 按约定 means as agreed. The thing agreed is the 约定.
column4: 我们约定明天下午三点见面。
column5: 我們約定明天下午三點見面。
column6: Wǒmen yuēdìng míngtiān xiàwǔ sān diǎn jiànmiàn.
column7: We agreed to meet at three tomorrow afternoon.
column9: A verb and a noun: you 約定 a time or place with someone, and 按約定 means as agreed. The thing agreed is the 約定.

column3: A verb and a noun, weightier than 答应: 做出承诺 is to make a promise and 信守承诺 is to keep it. 承 pictures a kneeling person and two hands, in the sense of holding or carrying.
column4: 他承诺下个月还钱。
column5: 他承諾下個月還錢。
column6: Tā chéngnuò xià ge yuè huán qián.
column7: He promised to pay the money back next month.
column9: A verb and a noun, weightier than 答應: 做出承諾 is to make a promise and 信守承諾 is to keep it. 承 pictures a kneeling person and two hands, in the sense of holding or carrying.

column3: A limited number of places for an admission, a job, a trip or a competition: 名额有限 means places are limited, and 名额已满 means they are full.
column4: 这次比赛的名额只有十个。
column5: 這次比賽的名額只有十個。
column6: Zhè cì bǐsài de míng'é zhǐ yǒu shí gè.
column7: There are only ten places in this competition.
column9: A limited number of places for an admission, a job, a trip or a competition: 名額有限 means places are limited, and 名額已滿 means they are full.

column3: Mostly in 以……的名义 (in the name of) and 名义上 (in name only, on paper), which hints that reality differs: 名义上是经理 means titled manager but not really in charge.
column4: 他名义上是经理，其实什么都不管。
column5: 他名義上是經理，其實什麼都不管。
column6: Tā míngyì shàng shì jīnglǐ, qíshí shénme dōu bù guǎn.
column7: He is manager in name only and actually takes care of nothing.
column9: Mostly in 以……的名義 (in the name of) and 名義上 (in name only, on paper), which hints that reality differs: 名義上是經理 means titled manager but not really in charge.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 权力 (power you wield), 权利 (a right you hold), 人权, 版权, 投票权. Alone it appears mainly after 有 or 无, for having or lacking the right to do something.
column4: 你有权知道真相。
column5: 你有權知道真相。
column6: Nǐ yǒu quán zhīdào zhēnxiàng.
column7: You have the right to know the truth.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 權力 (power you wield), 權利 (a right you hold), 人權, 版權, 投票權. Alone it appears mainly after 有 or 無, for having or lacking the right to do something.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 负责 (take charge of), 负担 (a burden), 负伤 (get wounded). It also means negative, as in 负数 and 负面, the opposite of 正.
column4: 我们队三胜一负。
column5: 我們隊三勝一負。
column6: Wǒmen duì sān shèng yī fù.
column7: Our team won three and lost one.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 負責 (take charge of), 負擔 (a burden), 負傷 (get wounded). It also means negative, as in 負數 and 負面, the opposite of 正.

column3: To hand something in to a person or body that will process it: 提交报告, 提交申请, 提交作业. It is also the Submit button on a web form.
column4: 请在周五前提交申请表。
column5: 請在週五前提交申請表。
column6: Qǐng zài zhōu wǔ qián tíjiāo shēnqǐng biǎo.
column7: Please submit the application form before Friday.
column9: To hand something in to a person or body that will process it: 提交報告, 提交申請, 提交作業. It is also the Submit button on a web form.

column3: To book a slot with a person or service, such as a doctor, a haircut or a visit; it is also the noun, a booking. For hotel rooms and tickets, 预订 is the usual word.
column4: 我已经预约了牙医。
column5: 我已經預約了牙醫。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng yùyuē le yáyī.
column7: I have already booked an appointment with the dentist.
column9: To book a slot with a person or service, such as a doctor, a haircut or a visit; it is also the noun, a booking. For hotel rooms and tickets, 預訂 is the usual word.

column3: A formal alliance of countries, companies or groups. Related words: 盟友 (an ally) and 结盟 (to form an alliance).
column4: 这两个国家结成了联盟。
column5: 這兩個國家結成了聯盟。
column6: Zhè liǎng gè guójiā jiéchéng le liánméng.
column7: These two countries formed an alliance.
column9: A formal alliance of countries, companies or groups. Related words: 盟友 (an ally) and 結盟 (to form an alliance).

column3: A political party, mostly in compounds: 政党, 党员 (a party member), 民主党. On the mainland, 党 alone usually means the Communist Party.
column4: 这个国家有两个大党。
column5: 這個國家有兩個大黨。
column6: Zhège guójiā yǒu liǎng gè dà dǎng.
column7: This country has two major parties.
column9: A political party, mostly in compounds: 政黨, 黨員 (a party member), 民主黨. On the mainland, 黨 alone usually means the Communist Party.

column3: The ruling power seen as a system, a regime: 夺取政权 is to seize power and 新政权 a new regime. 政府 is the government as the body that administers.
column4: 这个政权维持了三十年。
column5: 這個政權維持了三十年。
column6: Zhège zhèngquán wéichí le sānshí nián.
column7: This regime lasted thirty years.
column9: The ruling power seen as a system, a regime: 奪取政權 is to seize power and 新政權 a new regime. 政府 is the government as the body that administers.

column3: In practice used mainly for the prime ministers of Japan and the UK; for most other countries the word is 总理. Read xiàng, 相 can mean a government minister; read xiāng it means each other.
column4: 日本首相今天访问了中国。
column5: 日本首相今天訪問了中國。
column6: Rìběn shǒuxiàng jīntiān fǎngwèn le Zhōngguó.
column7: The Japanese prime minister visited China today.
column9: In practice used mainly for the prime ministers of Japan and the UK; for most other countries the word is 總理. Read xiàng, 相 can mean a government minister; read xiāng it means each other.

column3: Goes right before a title to mean the top one: 首席执行官 (CEO), 首席代表, 首席记者, 首席小提琴手 (concertmaster). 席 began as a picture of a woven mat with ornament; its meanings include woven mat and seat.
column4: 她是乐团的首席小提琴手。
column5: 她是樂團的首席小提琴手。
column6: Tā shì yuètuán de shǒuxí xiǎotíqín shǒu.
column7: She is the concertmaster of the orchestra.
column9: Goes right before a title to mean the top one: 首席執行官 (CEO), 首席代表, 首席記者, 首席小提琴手 (concertmaster). 席 began as a picture of a woven mat with ornament; its meanings include woven mat and seat.

column3: An ambassador, the head of an embassy: 驻华大使 is the ambassador to China. Also a goodwill or brand figure, as in 形象大使. In 使 the 吏 is the sound part, but it also represents a hand holding perhaps a flag, to mean "representative, ambassador".
column4: 大使今天会见了外交部长。
column5: 大使今天會見了外交部長。
column6: Dàshǐ jīntiān huìjiàn le wàijiāo bùzhǎng.
column7: The ambassador met the foreign minister today.
column9: An ambassador, the head of an embassy: 駐華大使 is the ambassador to China. Also a goodwill or brand figure, as in 形象大使. In 使 the 吏 is the sound part, but it also represents a hand holding perhaps a flag, to mean "representative, ambassador".

column3: On the mainland, the police: 公安局 is the local police bureau, and 公安 also names the officers. Elsewhere it just means public safety.
column4: 他被公安带走了。
column5: 他被公安帶走了。
column6: Tā bèi gōng'ān dàizǒu le.
column7: He was taken away by the police.
column9: On the mainland, the police: 公安局 is the local police bureau, and 公安 also names the officers. Elsewhere it just means public safety.

column3: Both a high-rise (高层建筑) and the upper ranks of an organization (公司高层, top management), the opposite of 基层, the lower ranks. 高 began as a picture of a tall building.
column4: 公司高层决定裁员。
column5: 公司高層決定裁員。
column6: Gōngsī gāocéng juédìng cáiyuán.
column7: The company's top management decided to lay off staff.
column9: Both a high-rise (高層建築) and the upper ranks of an organization (公司高層, top management), the opposite of 基層, the lower ranks. 高 began as a picture of a tall building.

column3: Besides public (公园, 公共), 公 marks a male animal, as in 公鸡 and 公牛, with 母 for the female. One traditional account, disputed in modern times, reads 公 as 八 (opposite) over 厶 (private): the opposite of private, so public.
column4: 这只狗是公的。
column5: 這隻狗是公的。
column6: Zhè zhī gǒu shì gōng de.
column7: This dog is male.
column9: Besides public (公園, 公共), 公 marks a male animal, as in 公雞 and 公牛, with 母 for the female. One traditional account, disputed in modern times, reads 公 as 八 (opposite) over 厶 (private): the opposite of private, so public.

column3: A formal, cultural name for China, found in 中华文化, 中华民族 and the full name 中华人民共和国, and also in the Republic of China (中华民国). Related: 华人 and 华语.
column4: 中华文化源远流长。
column5: 中華文化源遠流長。
column6: Zhōnghuá wénhuà yuányuǎn liúcháng.
column7: Chinese culture has a long history.
column9: A formal, cultural name for China, found in 中華文化, 中華民族 and the full name 中華人民共和國, and also in the Republic of China (中華民國). Related: 華人 and 華語.

column3: As a suffix 族 names a group of people by a shared job or habit: 上班族 are office workers, 月光族 people who spend their whole paycheck every month. It is built from a flag and an arrow.
column4: 他是一个普通的上班族。
column5: 他是一個普通的上班族。
column6: Tā shì yī gè pǔtōng de shàngbān zú.
column7: He is an ordinary office worker.
column9: As a suffix 族 names a group of people by a shared job or habit: 上班族 are office workers, 月光族 people who spend their whole paycheck every month. It is built from a flag and an arrow.

column3: The everyday sense is to cover or veil, as in 蒙住眼睛; in formal words it means to suffer or receive: 蒙受损失 is to suffer a loss, and 承蒙 opens a polite thank-you. Read mēng, the same character means knocked unconscious or dazed.
column4: 公司蒙受了很大的损失。
column5: 公司蒙受了很大的損失。
column6: Gōngsī méng shòu le hěn dà de sǔnshī.
column7: The company suffered a big loss.
column9: The everyday sense is to cover or veil, as in 蒙住眼睛; in formal words it means to suffer or receive: 蒙受損失 is to suffer a loss, and 承蒙 opens a polite thank-you. Read mēng, the same character means knocked unconscious or dazed.

column3: Added to a field, 界 means everyone and everything in it: 政界 is the political world, 教育界 education circles, 娱乐界 show business.
column4: 他在教育界工作了三十年。
column5: 他在教育界工作了三十年。
column6: Tā zài jiàoyù jiè gōngzuò le sānshí nián.
column7: He has worked in education for thirty years.
column9: Added to a field, 界 means everyone and everything in it: 政界 is the political world, 教育界 education circles, 娛樂界 show business.

column3: Used for finding people by tests or competition, for a team or a post: 选拔人才, and 选拔赛 is a qualifying round.
column4: 学校从全校学生中选拔了十名运动员。
column5: 學校從全校學生中選拔了十名運動員。
column6: Xuéxiào cóng quán xiào xuéshēng zhōng xuǎnbá le shí míng yùndòngyuán.
column7: The school selected ten athletes from all its students.
column9: Used for finding people by tests or competition, for a team or a post: 選拔人才, and 選拔賽 is a qualifying round.

column3: Used for prizes and honors: a panel or the public judges the candidates and picks the winners, as in 评选最佳影片. For picking people for a team or post, 选拔 is the word.
column4: 这部电影被评选为年度最佳影片。
column5: 這部電影被評選為年度最佳影片。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng bèi píngxuǎn wéi niándù zuìjiā yǐngpiàn.
column7: This film was chosen as the best film of the year.
column9: Used for prizes and honors: a panel or the public judges the candidates and picks the winners, as in 評選最佳影片. For picking people for a team or post, 選拔 is the word.

column3: Common in news and politics: 民意调查 is an opinion poll, and leaders 顺应民意 or 违背民意. In Taiwan 民意代表 also means an elected lawmaker.
column4: 政府应该倾听民意。
column5: 政府應該傾聽民意。
column6: Zhèngfǔ yīnggāi qīngtīng mínyì.
column7: The government should listen to public opinion.
column9: Common in news and politics: 民意調查 is an opinion poll, and leaders 順應民意 or 違背民意. In Taiwan 民意代表 also means an elected lawmaker.

column3: A formal word of news and notices: 公众场合 are public places, and 公众人物 is a public figure.
column4: 在公众场合请保持安静。
column5: 在公眾場合請保持安靜。
column6: Zài gōngzhòng chǎnghé qǐng bǎochí ānjìng.
column7: Please keep quiet in public places.
column9: A formal word of news and notices: 公眾場合 are public places, and 公眾人物 is a public figure.

column3: Besides the main stream of a river, it is the mainstream in a figurative sense: 主流媒体 is mainstream media, and 非主流 means alternative or offbeat.
column4: 这种音乐已经成为主流。
column5: 這種音樂已經成為主流。
column6: Zhè zhǒng yīnyuè yǐjīng chéngwéi zhǔliú.
column7: This kind of music has become mainstream.
column9: Besides the main stream of a river, it is the mainstream in a figurative sense: 主流媒體 is mainstream media, and 非主流 means alternative or offbeat.

column3: A strong, moral word for sin or wickedness as such. A specific criminal act is 罪行, and 犯罪 is to commit a crime. 罪恶感 is a feeling of guilt.
column4: 他的罪恶终于被揭露了。
column5: 他的罪惡終於被揭露了。
column6: Tā de zuì'è zhōngyú bèi jiēlù le.
column7: His wrongdoing was finally exposed.
column9: A strong, moral word for sin or wickedness as such. A specific criminal act is 罪行, and 犯罪 is to commit a crime. 罪惡感 is a feeling of guilt.

column3: The person who did a killing, not any criminal: 罪犯 is the general word. Police look for the 凶手, and 真凶 is the real culprit.
column4: 警察终于抓到了凶手。
column5: 警察終於抓到了兇手。
column6: Jǐngchá zhōngyú zhuā dào le xiōngshǒu.
column7: The police finally caught the murderer.
column9: The person who did a killing, not any criminal: 罪犯 is the general word. Police look for the 兇手, and 真兇 is the real culprit.

column3: An authority takes things away: a teacher, customs or the police. 没收财产 is to confiscate property.
column4: 手机被老师没收了。
column5: 手機被老師沒收了。
column6: Shǒujī bèi lǎoshī mòshōu le.
column7: The teacher confiscated my phone.
column9: An authority takes things away: a teacher, customs or the police. 沒收財產 is to confiscate property.

column3: It takes rights, privacy or territory as its object: 侵犯隐私 violates privacy, 侵犯版权 infringes a copyright, 侵犯领土 violates territory.
column4: 这样做侵犯了他的隐私。
column5: 這樣做侵犯了他的隱私。
column6: Zhèyàng zuò qīnfàn le tā de yǐnsī.
column7: Doing this violated his privacy.
column9: It takes rights, privacy or territory as its object: 侵犯隱私 violates privacy, 侵犯版權 infringes a copyright, 侵犯領土 violates territory.

column3: Usually critical: meddling in what is not your business, whether a parent in a child's choices or a country in another's internal affairs (干涉内政). 涉 also means to be involved or concerned.
column4: 父母不应该过多干涉孩子的选择。
column5: 父母不應該過多干涉孩子的選擇。
column6: Fùmǔ bù yīnggāi guòduō gānshè háizi de xuǎnzé.
column7: Parents should not interfere too much in their children's choices.
column9: Usually critical: meddling in what is not your business, whether a parent in a child's choices or a country in another's internal affairs (干涉內政). 涉 also means to be involved or concerned.

column3: Describes illegal copies of software, discs, books and films: 盗版软件. The genuine item is 正版.
column4: 这个软件是盗版的。
column5: 這個軟件是盜版的。
column6: Zhège ruǎnjiàn shì dàobǎn de.
column7: This software is pirated.
column9: Describes illegal copies of software, discs, books and films: 盜版軟件. The genuine item is 正版.

column3: The party sued in court, the other side of 原告. 被 marks the passive, so it is literally the one who is sued.
column4: 被告在法庭上否认了指控。
column5: 被告在法庭上否認了指控。
column6: Bèigào zài fǎtíng shàng fǒurèn le zhǐkòng.
column7: The defendant denied the charges in court.
column9: The party sued in court, the other side of 原告. 被 marks the passive, so it is literally the one who is sued.

column3: The side that brings the case, set against 被告. 原 is "original": the party that first brought the suit.
column4: 原告要求被告赔偿损失。
column5: 原告要求被告賠償損失。
column6: Yuángào yāoqiú bèigào péicháng sǔnshī.
column7: The plaintiff demanded that the defendant pay for the losses.
column9: The side that brings the case, set against 被告. 原 is "original": the party that first brought the suit.

column3: Formal and legal: a person or company sues someone, or prosecutors charge a suspect (检察院起诉). In plain speech 告 is the everyday verb, as in 我要告你.
column4: 他决定起诉那家公司。
column5: 他決定起訴那家公司。
column6: Tā juédìng qǐsù nà jiā gōngsī.
column7: He decided to sue that company.
column9: Formal and legal: a person or company sues someone, or prosecutors charge a suspect (檢察院起訴). In plain speech 告 is the everyday verb, as in 我要告你.

column3: A verb plus object that can be split: 打了一场官司, 打赢官司 to win a case, 打输官司 to lose one. 打 is the light verb of 打电话 and 打球.
column4: 他为了房子跟邻居打官司。
column5: 他為了房子跟鄰居打官司。
column6: Tā wèile fángzi gēn línjū dǎguānsi.
column7: He is fighting his neighbor in court over the house.
column9: A verb plus object that can be split: 打了一場官司, 打贏官司 to win a case, 打輸官司 to lose one. 打 is the light verb of 打電話 and 打球.

column3: Counted with 场, and goes with 打, 赢 and 输: 一场官司, 赢了官司. 吃官司 is informal for landing in legal trouble.
column4: 这场官司打了三年。
column5: 這場官司打了三年。
column6: Zhè chǎng guānsi dǎ le sān nián.
column7: This lawsuit has dragged on for three years.
column9: Counted with 場, and goes with 打, 贏 and 輸: 一場官司, 贏了官司. 吃官司 is informal for landing in legal trouble.

column3: The courtroom and the hearing held there: 上法庭 to go to court, 出庭 to appear in court. The court as an institution is 法院.
column4: 证人在法庭上作证。
column5: 證人在法庭上作證。
column6: Zhèngrén zài fǎtíng shàng zuòzhèng.
column7: The witness testified in court.
column9: The courtroom and the hearing held there: 上法庭 to go to court, 出庭 to appear in court. The court as an institution is 法院.

column3: A court or referee gives a ruling: 判刑 to sentence, 判决 a verdict. It also forms 判断, to judge or tell something from evidence.
column4: 法院判他三年有期徒刑。
column5: 法院判他三年有期徒刑。
column6: Fǎyuàn pàn tā sān nián yǒuqī túxíng.
column7: The court sentenced him to three years in prison.
column9: A court or referee gives a ruling: 判刑 to sentence, 判決 a verdict. It also forms 判斷, to judge or tell something from evidence.

column3: A dispute with a concrete cause, between people, firms or groups: 经济纠纷, 劳动纠纷. It goes with 解决 and 调解 (to mediate).
column4: 两家公司因为合同发生了纠纷。
column5: 兩家公司因為合同發生了糾紛。
column6: Liǎng jiā gōngsī yīnwèi hétong fāshēng le jiūfēn.
column7: The two companies got into a dispute over the contract.
column9: A dispute with a concrete cause, between people, firms or groups: 經濟糾紛, 勞動糾紛. It goes with 解決 and 調解 (to mediate).

column3: Aimed at a fault or a past event: 追究责任 means to hold someone responsible, 追究原因 to look into the cause. Taiwan reads 究 as jiù, not jiū.
column4: 这件事我们一定会追究到底。
column5: 這件事我們一定會追究到底。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒmen yīdìng huì zhuījiū dào dǐ.
column7: We will definitely get to the bottom of this.
column9: Aimed at a fault or a past event: 追究責任 means to hold someone responsible, 追究原因 to look into the cause. Taiwan reads 究 as jiù, not jiū.

column3: Goes with official or formal things you take back: a charge, an order, a decision, a permit. The 撤 is pulling back, as in 撤退 and 撤离.
column4: 法院撤销了原来的判决。
column5: 法院撤銷了原來的判決。
column6: Fǎyuàn chèxiāo le yuánlái de pànjué.
column7: The court revoked the original ruling.
column9: Goes with official or formal things you take back: a charge, an order, a decision, a permit. The 撤 is pulling back, as in 撤退 and 撤離.

column3: The word for something that is no longer valid: tickets, coupons, forms, contracts. It is printed on them, as in 过期作废, void after the expiration date.
column4: 这张票过期就作废了。
column5: 這張票過期就作廢了。
column6: Zhè zhāng piào guòqī jiù zuòfèi le.
column7: This ticket becomes void once it expires.
column9: The word for something that is no longer valid: tickets, coupons, forms, contracts. It is printed on them, as in 過期作廢, void after the expiration date.

column3: 舰 is a large naval ship and turns up in other naval words: 战舰, 舰队, 航空母舰. For an ordinary ship, use 船.
column4: 一艘军舰驶进了港口。
column5: 一艘軍艦駛進了港口。
column6: Yī sōu jūnjiàn shǐ jìn le gǎngkǒu.
column7: A warship sailed into the harbor.
column9: 艦 is a large naval ship and turns up in other naval words: 戰艦, 艦隊, 航空母艦. For an ordinary ship, use 船.

column3: Also a verb in chess and in figures of speech: 将他一军 puts him on the spot, with a challenge he has to answer.
column4: 这位将军指挥了那场战斗。
column5: 這位將軍指揮了那場戰鬥。
column6: Zhè wèi jiāngjūn zhǐhuī le nà chǎng zhàndòu.
column7: This general commanded that battle.
column9: Also a verb in chess and in figures of speech: 將他一軍 puts him on the spot, with a challenge he has to answer.

column3: Used literally for the troops at the front and figuratively for a trailblazer in any field: 改革先锋. 先锋队 is a vanguard unit, and 先锋派 is the avant-garde.
column4: 他是改革的先锋。
column5: 他是改革的先鋒。
column6: Tā shì gǎigé de xiānfēng.
column7: He is a pioneer of reform.
column9: Used literally for the troops at the front and figuratively for a trailblazer in any field: 改革先鋒. 先鋒隊 is a vanguard unit, and 先鋒派 is the avant-garde.

column3: Soldiers who served or fought together. It also reaches people who have been through hard times side by side, and old comrades keep using it for each other for life. An old explanation reads 友 as two hands, so friendship.
column4: 他们是多年的战友。
column5: 他們是多年的戰友。
column6: Tāmen shì duō nián de zhànyǒu.
column7: They have been comrades-in-arms for many years.
column9: Soldiers who served or fought together. It also reaches people who have been through hard times side by side, and old comrades keep using it for each other for life. An old explanation reads 友 as two hands, so friendship.

column3: 驻 is followed by the place where someone is stationed, as in 驻外 and 驻法国大使, and it forms 驻军 (stationed troops) and 驻扎.
column4: 他是驻法国的大使。
column5: 他是駐法國的大使。
column6: Tā shì zhù Fǎguó de dàshǐ.
column7: He is the ambassador to France.
column9: 駐 is followed by the place where someone is stationed, as in 駐外 and 駐法國大使, and it forms 駐軍 (stationed troops) and 駐紮.

column3: It covers military operations, as a verb (在前线作战) or before a noun (作战计划). For a street fight, say 打架 instead.
column4: 他们在前线作战。
column5: 他們在前線作戰。
column6: Tāmen zài qiánxiàn zuòzhàn.
column7: They are fighting at the front.
column9: It covers military operations, as a verb (在前線作戰) or before a noun (作戰計劃). For a street fight, say 打架 instead.

column3: The big-picture, long-range plan, while 战术 is the tactics used within a fight. It is used well beyond war: 发展战略 is a development strategy, and companies have a 战略 too.
column4: 公司制定了新的发展战略。
column5: 公司制定了新的發展戰略。
column6: Gōngsī zhìdìng le xīn de fāzhǎn zhànlüè.
column7: The company drew up a new development strategy.
column9: The big-picture, long-range plan, while 戰術 is the tactics used within a fight. It is used well beyond war: 發展戰略 is a development strategy, and companies have a 戰略 too.

column3: The tactics used within a fight or a game, a step below 战略; sports coverage uses it a lot. This 术 is skill or method, as in 技术 and 艺术.
column4: 教练改变了比赛的战术。
column5: 教練改變了比賽的戰術。
column6: Jiàoliàn gǎibiàn le bǐsài de zhànshù.
column7: The coach changed the tactics for the game.
column9: The tactics used within a fight or a game, a step below 戰略; sports coverage uses it a lot. This 術 is skill or method, as in 技術 and 藝術.

column3: A straight, double-edged blade, unlike the single-edged 刀. It turns up in 击剑 (fencing) and 剑道, and a 剑客 is a swordsman.
column4: 他手里拿着一把剑。
column5: 他手裡拿著一把劍。
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ názhe yī bǎ jiàn.
column7: He is holding a sword.
column9: A straight, double-edged blade, unlike the single-edged 刀. It turns up in 擊劍 (fencing) and 劍道, and a 劍客 is a swordsman.

column3: Covers physical attacks and also verbal ones (攻击别人的观点), and cyberattacks too: 网络攻击. Taiwan reads the second syllable jí.
column4: 对方的攻击很猛烈。
column5: 對方的攻擊很猛烈。
column6: Duìfāng de gōngjī hěn měngliè.
column7: The other side's attack was fierce.
column9: Covers physical attacks and also verbal ones (攻擊別人的觀點), and cyberattacks too: 網絡攻擊. Taiwan reads the second syllable jí.

column3: Beyond real bombs: 定时炸弹 is a time bomb and also a hidden danger, and 重磅炸弹 is a bombshell of news.
column4: 警察拆除了一枚炸弹。
column5: 警察拆除了一枚炸彈。
column6: Jǐngchá chāichú le yī méi zhàdàn.
column7: The police defused a bomb.
column9: Beyond real bombs: 定時炸彈 is a time bomb and also a hidden danger, and 重磅炸彈 is a bombshell of news.

column3: The explosive material itself, such as dynamite, while 炸弹 is the finished bomb that holds it. 药 is not only medicine: it also covers a substance used for a specific purpose, such as poisoning, explosion or fermenting.
column4: 工人用炸药开山。
column5: 工人用炸藥開山。
column6: Gōngrén yòng zhàyào kāi shān.
column7: The workers blast the mountain with explosives.
column9: The explosive material itself, such as dynamite, while 炸彈 is the finished bomb that holds it. 藥 is not only medicine: it also covers a substance used for a specific purpose, such as poisoning, explosion or fermenting.

column3: Takes sudden big events or feelings as its subject: 战争, 火山, 疫情 or a person's anger all 爆发. It is also used of a burst of strength. The 暴 in it originally meant "violence", which may add to the meaning.
column4: 战争在那年爆发了。
column5: 戰爭在那年爆發了。
column6: Zhànzhēng zài nà nián bàofā le.
column7: The war broke out that year.
column9: Takes sudden big events or feelings as its subject: 戰爭, 火山, 疫情 or a person's anger all 爆發. It is also used of a burst of strength. The 暴 in it originally meant "violence", which may add to the meaning.

column3: Used for waves pounding a shore and, more often, for a shock to something larger: 受到冲击 means to be hit hard, and 冲击波 is a shock wave.
column4: 这件事对经济造成了很大的冲击。
column5: 這件事對經濟造成了很大的衝擊。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì duì jīngjì zàochéng le hěn dà de chōngjī.
column7: This event had a big impact on the economy.
column9: Used for waves pounding a shore and, more often, for a shock to something larger: 受到衝擊 means to be hit hard, and 衝擊波 is a shock wave.

column3: Goes with weighty goals won by effort: 夺取胜利, 夺取政权, 夺取冠军. A thief who grabs a purse is 抢, not 夺取.
column4: 为了夺取冠军，他们每天训练。
column5: 為了奪取冠軍，他們每天訓練。
column6: Wèile duóqǔ guànjūn, tāmen měitiān xùnliàn.
column7: To win the championship, they train every day.
column9: Goes with weighty goals won by effort: 奪取勝利, 奪取政權, 奪取冠軍. A thief who grabs a purse is 搶, not 奪取.

column3: Both sides go after the same thing: 争夺冠军, 争夺市场, 争夺权力. The object is something prized and limited.
column4: 两支球队争夺冠军。
column5: 兩支球隊爭奪冠軍。
column6: Liǎng zhī qiúduì zhēngduó guànjūn.
column7: The two teams are fighting for the championship.
column9: Both sides go after the same thing: 爭奪冠軍, 爭奪市場, 爭奪權力. The object is something prized and limited.

column3: For troops taking a place and for holding a spot: 占据城市, 占据市场, and 占据主导地位, to hold the dominant position.
column4: 敌军占据了这座城市。
column5: 敵軍佔據了這座城市。
column6: Díjūn zhànjù le zhè zuò chéngshì.
column7: The enemy army occupied this city.
column9: For troops taking a place and for holding a spot: 佔據城市, 佔據市場, and 佔據主導地位, to hold the dominant position.

column3: Leaving a dangerous place, often as an order in news reports: 紧急撤离 is an emergency evacuation, and people 撤离 a disaster zone.
column4: 居民已经全部撤离了灾区。
column5: 居民已經全部撤離了災區。
column6: Jūmín yǐjīng quánbù chèlí le zāiqū.
column7: The residents have all been evacuated from the disaster area.
column9: Leaving a dangerous place, often as an order in news reports: 緊急撤離 is an emergency evacuation, and people 撤離 a disaster zone.

column3: Mostly paired with a partner: 毁坏 and 摧毁 for damage, 毁灭 for total ruin. It also means to slander, as in 毁谤.
column4: 大火毁了整座房子。
column5: 大火毀了整座房子。
column6: Dàhuǒ huǐ le zhěng zuò fángzi.
column7: The fire destroyed the whole house.
column9: Mostly paired with a partner: 毀壞 and 摧毀 for damage, 毀滅 for total ruin. It also means to slander, as in 毀謗.

column3: 灭火 puts out a fire, 灯灭了 means the light went out, and 消灭 wipes something out.
column4: 消防员在灭火。
column5: 消防員在滅火。
column6: Xiāofángyuán zài miè huǒ.
column7: The firefighters are putting out the fire.
column9: 滅火 puts out a fire, 燈滅了 means the light went out, and 消滅 wipes something out.
